Values

The value layer preserves both mathematical content and source representation. A decimal retains its scale and special-value payload, a temporal retains its written form, and a binary value distinguishes exact from nearest reading. We call this boundary the representation-fidelity boundary (RFB). The RFB separates chronological or numeric comparison from representation equality and makes each loss of source information explicit.

This page states 41 registered laws for (i) representation and coercion, (ii) binary and decimal operations, (iii) temporal values, (iv) byte-text mappings, and (v) expression evaluation. Its base finite scopes contain 600 signed numerals with at most two significand digits and exponents from -1 through 1, all 65,536 binary16 patterns, 19,098 temporal lexemes, and all 65,793 byte strings of length at most two. Focused tests add separate products for special decimals, epoch boundaries, and written temporal forms, and the temporal order laws extend the 19,098 lexemes by the offsets -04:56:02 and +05:30:00 and by the unwritten offsets of 0 and +05:30. Each audit remains open until its named exhaustive and property differentials and mutation campaigns pass and its independent proof reviewer signs off at the same immutable commit.

One term is a definition rather than a law. Under a column’s nearest-keeping-lexeme reading, coerce returns the nearest value of the column’s width and keeps no lexeme itself; the source text the value was read from is kept by the reading route, in its complement, and the route writes it back byte for byte while the cell is unedited. We call that kept text the nearest-reading complement of the cell. Its round trip is a law of the route that keeps it, stated with that route; on this page the value layer’s part is the nearest-reading acceptance law, which gives the value the kept text denotes.

Every operational claim below uses the resource-success premise (Premise A): each requested collection length is representable on the target, and each allocation succeeds. A capacity overflow, stack exhaustion or allocator termination is a process failure, not a Result or Option outcome of the value operation. Thus a claim that an operation returns is a claim about executions satisfying Premise A; the finite executable counterparts establish this premise through their explicit bounds.

Representation equality is canonical-byte equality

Statement

Let D be the encoder domain: the set of reference values v (type Value) for which value_bytes(v) is Some. For all values l,r:

  1. representation(l, r) is None exactly when l∈/D or r∈/D, and for l,r∈D it is Some(b) with b true exactly when value_bytes(l) and value_bytes(r) are the same byte string. Representation equality, written l≈r, is the relation representation(l, r) = Some(true).
  2. v∈D exactly when write_temporal returns Some for every temporal occurring in v: v itself when it is a Temporal, and every temporal reachable from v through the fields of an Opaque, the fields of an Unknown and the items of a List, at any depth. In particular every value containing no temporal is in D.
  3. On D, ≈ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and l=r under the derived structural equality of Value implies l≈r.
  4. On D, two values whose outermost variants differ are never representation equal; Float(a) ≈ Float(b) exactly when the 64-bit patterns a and b are equal (so 0.0 and -0.0 differ, and two NaNs are equal exactly when their patterns are); Int(a) ≈ Int(b) exactly when a=b; Bool(a) ≈ Bool(b) exactly when a=b; and LabeledNull(a) ≈ LabeledNull(b) exactly when a=b.

The production relation, equality of Value::canonical_bytes (equivalently Value::canonical_cmp returning Equal), is required to agree with ≈ on the images of values in D, as the named differential tests check.

Outside the domain

A pair in which some value lies outside D has no reference result: representation returns None, and there is no typed refusal, since the operation is a predicate. By clause 2, this happens exactly when the value contains a temporal that write_temporal refuses, namely one that is not well_formed, one whose form() is None outside the complete layout, or a time-form infinity. The production canonical_bytes is total, so the differential comparison is made only on pairs for which the reference returns Some.

Definitions used

  • Value is the reference instance value of panproto_reference::value, with sixteen variants; its derived equality compares variants and payloads structurally, and a Float payload is its binary64 bit pattern, so two floats are structurally equal exactly when their patterns are.
  • Writer is a growable byte string with primitive writers: tag(t) appends the one byte t; u64(x) and i64(x) append the eight little-endian bytes of x (to_le_bytes); raw(b) appends the length of b as u64 and then b; str(s) is raw of the UTF-8 bytes of s. None of them can fail.
  • write_value(w, v) appends a variant tag byte (0 Bool, 1 Int, 2 Float, 3 Str, 4 Bytes, 5 CidLink, 6 Blob, 7 Token, 8 Null, 9 Opaque, 10 Unknown, 11 List, 12 LabeledNull, 13 Decimal, 14 BigInt, 15 Temporal) and then the payload; it returns Option<()> and propagates None from write_map, from a recursive write_value on a List item, and from write_temporal.
  • write_map(w, m) writes the entry count and then, in ascending key order, each key by str and each value by write_value, propagating None.
  • value_bytes(v) runs write_value on a fresh Writer and returns Some of the bytes, or None when write_value returns None.
  • representation(l, r) is defined as Some(value_bytes(l)? == value_bytes(r)?), where ? returns None from the function when its operand is None.

Proof

  1. By the definition of representation, the first ? returns None when value_bytes(l) is None, the second returns None when value_bytes(r) is None, and otherwise the result is Some of the byte-string equality of the two encodings. With D defined as the set on which value_bytes is Some, this is clause 1.
  2. Clause 2 holds by structural induction on v, over the sixteen arms of write_value. The arms Bool, Int, Float, Str, Bytes, CidLink, Blob, Token, Null and LabeledNull call only the primitive writers, which cannot fail; the arms Decimal and BigInt call write_decimal and write_bigint, which return () and call only primitive writers. Each of these twelve arms returns Some, and the value contains no temporal. The arm Temporal returns Some exactly when write_temporal does. The arms Opaque and Unknown return Some exactly when write_map does, which by its definition holds exactly when write_value returns Some on every field value; the arm List returns Some exactly when write_value returns Some on every item. Field values and items are proper subterms of v, so by the induction hypothesis each returns Some exactly when every temporal it contains is accepted by write_temporal, and the temporals of v are exactly the temporals of those subterms. Since value_bytes(v) is Some exactly when write_value returns Some, clause 2 follows.
  3. For clause 3, value_bytes is a function of its argument: it starts from an empty Writer and its output depends only on v. Hence l=r gives value_bytes(l) = value_bytes(r), and by step 1 l≈r for l,r∈D; with r=l this is reflexivity. Symmetry and transitivity of ≈ on D follow from step 1, because ≈ is there the equality of byte strings, which is symmetric and transitive.
  4. For the first part of clause 4, the first byte that write_value appends is the variant tag, and the sixteen tags listed above are pairwise distinct. Two values with different outermost variants thus have encodings that differ at their first byte, and by step 1 they are not representation equal.
  5. For the remaining parts of clause 4, the encodings are: Float(a) gives the byte 2 followed by the eight bytes of a.to_le_bytes(); Int(a) gives 1 followed by a.to_le_bytes(); LabeledNull(a) gives 12 followed by a.to_le_bytes(); Bool(a) gives 0 followed by u8::from(a). Each of to_le_bytes on u64 and on i64, and u8::from on bool, is injective (the first two are bijections onto [u8; 8], the third sends false to 0 and true to 1). Two encodings of one of these variants are equal exactly when their payload bytes are, hence exactly when the payloads are equal, and step 1 turns this into the stated equivalences. In particular 0.0 and -0.0 have patterns 0x0000000000000000 and 0x8000000000000000, which differ, and two NaNs are representation equal exactly when their patterns are.

Declared kinds determine lexical mappings

Statement

For every lexeme text t, lexical class c and value specification s (with kind k = s.kind), the reference coercion coerce(t, c, s) is determined by the first of the following rows that applies, whenever its evaluation returns.

  1. Null. If c = Null, the result is Some(Ok(Null)).
  2. Tagged. If c = Tagged(g), the result is coerce_tagged_open(t, g, s): for k= Any it is coerce(t, String, s), and for k = Any, with n = tag_name(g) (the tag without a leading tag:yaml.org,2002:, or else without a leading !!), it is Some(Ok(Null)) when n = null, coerce(t, c', ValueSpec::of(k')) when tagged_kind(n) = Some((k', c')), and Some(Ok(Opaque { type_: g, fields: { "value": Str(t) } })) otherwise.
  3. Dialect. If s.numeral = Some(d) and the dialect is relevant, that is R(c,k) holds where R(c,k) means “c = Number, or c = String and k is one of Int, BigInt, Float, Decimal”, the result is Some(Err(NotANumber)) when normalize_numeral(t, c, k, d) is None, and otherwise coerce(N, c, s') for the normalized text N, where s′ is s with numeral set to None. That second call is decided by row 4.
  4. Kind. Otherwise the result is the reader of k:
    • Any: Some(coerce_any(t, c)); Bool: Some(coerce_bool(t, c)).
    • Int { bits, signed }: with B = s.int_bits.unwrap_or(bits), None if B=0; else Some(Err(NotANumber)) if c∈{Bool, Bytes, DateTime}; else Some(coerce_int(t, Some((B, signed && !s.unsigned)))).
    • BigInt: the same class check, then Some(coerce_int(t, None)).
    • Float { bits }: None if bits is not 16, 32 or 64; else the same class check, then Some(coerce_float(t, f, s.float_reading)) with f the format of width bits.
    • Decimal: the same class check, then Some(coerce_decimal(t, s)), which reads only s.precision and s.scale.
    • Str and Token: Err(NotANumberForKind) for Number, Err(InvalidEncoding) for Bool, and otherwise Ok(Str(t)) or Ok(Token(t)).
    • Bytes(e): Err(NotANumberForKind) for Number, Err(InvalidEncoding) for Bool, and otherwise Ok(Bytes(decode_bytes(t, e))), or Err(InvalidEncoding) when decode_bytes is None.
    • Date, Time, DateTime: Err(NotANumberForKind) for Number, Err(InvalidTemporal) for Bool, and otherwise coerce_temporal(t, s), which reads only k and s.with_time_zone.

Each result of rows 3 and 4 other than None is wrapped in Some.

Parameter dependence. Let P(k) be the parameters a kind reads: P(Int)={int_bits, unsigned}, P(Float)={float_reading}, P(Decimal)={precision, scale}, P(Date)=P(Time)=P(DateTime)={with_time_zone}, and P(k)=∅ for every other kind (the kind’s own fields, bits, signed and the bytes encoding, belong to k itself). Let the effective class c∗ be String when c = Tagged(_) and k= Any, and c otherwise. If two specifications s1​,s2​ have the same kind k, agree on P(k), and either agree on numeral or R(c∗,k) fails, then coerce(t, c, s_1) and coerce(t, c, s_2) are equal. In particular, when c = Null, or c = Tagged(_) and k = Any, the result depends on no parameter of s at all.

Domain. Call s admissible when k is not Int with B=0 and not Float { bits } with bits outside {16,32,64}. For admissible s the result is never None. For inadmissible s the result is None exactly when c= Null and it is not the case that s.numeral = Some(d), R(c∗,k) holds and normalize_numeral(t, c*, k, d) is None; in that last case the result is Some(Err(NotANumber)).

The production coerce in crates/panproto-inst/src/value/coerce.rs is required to equal this definition on admissible specifications, value for value and refusal reason for refusal reason, as the named differential tests check.

Outside the domain

  • An inadmissible specification (an Int kind of effective width 0, or a float width other than 16, 32 or 64) has no reference result outside the cases named in the Domain clause; the reference returns None there. The production reading of such a specification is not compared.
  • Termination of the float readers is not part of this statement: the statement describes every result the definition returns.

Definitions used

  • ScalarKind, ValueSpec, LexClass and FidelityReason are the reference types of panproto_reference::coerce. A ValueSpec holds kind, precision, scale, with_time_zone, int_bits, unsigned, float_reading and numeral; ValueSpec::of(k) has kind k, every optional parameter None, unsigned false and the exact float reading.
  • coerce(t, c, s) is the reference definition read in its source order: the Null test, the Tagged test, the dialect test with numeric_kind (the four numeric kinds) and dialect_applies (which is R(c,k)), and the final match on s.kind, wrapped in Some, inside which numeric_class refuses the classes Bool, Bytes and DateTime with NotANumber.
  • coerce_tagged_open(t, g, s) returns coerce(t, String, s) when k= Any, and otherwise Null, coerce(t, c', ValueSpec::of(k')) for the pair (k′,c′) that tagged_kind gives the tag name, or the opaque value of the tag.
  • tagged_kind maps the tag names it knows to the kinds Bool, BigInt, Float { bits: 64 }, Decimal, Str, Bytes(Base64), Bytes(Hex), DateTime, Date and Time, and every other name to None.
  • tag_name(g) is g.strip_prefix("tag:yaml.org,2002:").or_else(|| g.strip_prefix("!!")).unwrap_or(g), and opaque_of(g, t) is Opaque { type_: g, fields: { "value": Str(t) } }.
  • Format::of_width(bits) is Some exactly for 16,32,64.
  • normalize_numeral, coerce_any, coerce_bool, coerce_int, coerce_float, coerce_decimal, decode_bytes and coerce_temporal are the reference readers named in the rows; each returns a Result (or, for normalize_numeral and decode_bytes, an Option) and none returns the Option layer of Coerced.

Proof

  1. Row 1: the first statement of coerce returns Some(Ok(Null)) when c = Null, before any parameter is read.
  2. Row 2: the second statement returns coerce_tagged_open(t, g, s) when c = Tagged(g); the first line of coerce_tagged_open returns coerce(t, String, s) when k= Any, and for k = Any the remaining lines compute tag_name(g), return Some(Ok(Null)) for the name null, return coerce(t, c', ValueSpec::of(k')) when tagged_kind gives (k′,c′), and return Some(Ok(opaque_of(g, t))), whose type is g as written and whose single field value is Str(t), for every other name.
  3. Row 3: past rows 1 and 2, c is neither Null nor Tagged. The definition computes numeric_kind and dialect_applies, which is R(c,k), and when s.numeral = Some(d) and R(c,k) hold it returns Some(Err(NotANumber)) if normalize_numeral(t, c, k, d) is None and otherwise coerce(N, c, s'). In that recursive call c is unchanged (so rows 1 and 2 do not apply) and s'.numeral is None (so row 3 does not apply), hence it is decided by row 4 with the kind and every other parameter of s.
  4. Row 4: otherwise the definition returns Some of the match on k, whose arms are exactly those listed. The two None exits are the explicit return None for B=0 in the Int arm and the ? on Format::of_width(bits) in the Float arm, which returns None exactly when bits is not 16, 32 or 64. Every other arm yields a Result, so the call returns Some of it.
  5. Parameter dependence, by the three possible call depths. A call with c = Null returns at row 1 without reading s. A call with c = Tagged(_) and k = Any reads only the tag and then calls coerce with ValueSpec::of(k') or with no specification, so its result does not depend on s. A call with c = Tagged(_) and k= Any becomes coerce(t, String, s), which is the case c∗= String below. For a call with c=c∗ not Null or Tagged: row 3 reads s.numeral only when R(c∗,k) holds, and normalize_numeral reads only t, c∗, k and the dialect; its recursive call passes s with numeral cleared, so for s1​,s2​ agreeing as assumed the two recursive specifications again agree on k and P(k). Row 4 reads, by inspection of each arm: nothing under Any, Bool, BigInt, Str, Token and Bytes(_) beyond k; int_bits and unsigned under Int; float_reading under Float; precision and scale (inside coerce_decimal) under Decimal; and k with with_time_zone (inside coerce_temporal) under the temporal kinds. These are exactly P(k), so the two results are equal.
  6. Domain, admissible s: by step 4 the only None exits are the two inadmissible ones. Row 3 recurses with the same kind and int_bits, so an admissible s stays admissible. Row 2 with k= Any recurses with s itself. Row 2 with k = Any recurses with ValueSpec::of(k') for a kind from tagged_kind, and none of those kinds is Int or a float of a width other than 64, so each is admissible. Hence no call returns None.
  7. Domain, inadmissible s, by cases on c. If c = Null, row 1 gives Some(Ok(Null)). Otherwise k is Int or Float, so k= Any and the call reaches rows 3 and 4 with class c∗ (directly, or through row 2 with c∗= String). If s.numeral = Some(d), R(c∗,k) holds and normalization fails, row 3 returns Some(Err(NotANumber)). In every other case the call reaches row 4 for kind k with the same int_bits and width, either directly or through the recursive call of row 3, and step 4 returns None there before any class check. This is the stated characterization.

Value conversion preserves exact values

Statement

Under Premise D below, let s be a value-admissible specification: admissible in the sense of L-values-2, and with the exact float reading when its kind is a float kind. Write k = s.kind. For every value v, coerce_value(v, s) is Some, and its result is as follows (notation in Definitions used).

  1. Open kind. If k = Any, the result is Ok(v).
  2. Float kinds. If k = Float { bits }, let f be the format of width bits.
    1. If v is an exact source or a finite Float, the result is Ok exactly when x(v)∈Vf​. It is then v itself when v is a Float, and otherwise Float(β) with decode(B64, β) = Finite { negative: σ(v), value: x(v) }. Otherwise the result is Err(Overflow) when round_to(f, x(v), σ(v)) is Overflow and Err(PrecisionExceeded { max: m_f }) when it is finite, with m16​=5, m32​=9, m64​=17.
    2. An infinite Float gives Ok(v). A NaN Float gives Ok(v) when the low 53−pf​ bits of its fraction field are zero (always, for f = binary64) and Err(NonFinite) otherwise.
    3. A special decimal (Decimal(Infinite { .. }) or Decimal(NaN { .. })) gives Err(NonFinite).
    4. Str(t) and Token(t) give the result of coerce(t, String, s_f), where sf​ is ValueSpec::of(k) with numeral set to s.numeral: with no dialect this is coerce_float(t, f, Exact), and with a dialect d it is Err(NotANumber) when normalize_numeral(t, String, k, d) is None and coerce_float(N, f, Exact) for the normalized text N otherwise. Every other value is read without the dialect: Bool(_) and Temporal(_) give Err(NotANumber); Null gives Ok(Null); every other value (Bytes, CidLink, Blob, Opaque, Unknown, List, LabeledNull) gives Ok(v).
  3. Other declared kinds. If k is neither Any nor a float kind:
    1. A non-finite Float gives Err(NonFinite), and so does a special decimal when k = BigInt.
    2. Otherwise, with s0​ the specification s with numeral set to None, the result is coerce(λ, c, s) when v is a Str or a Token and coerce(λ, c, s_0) for every other v, whenever lexeme_of(v, k) = Some((λ, c)); it is Ok(v) when lexeme_of(v, k) is None. A numeral dialect is thus applied only to source text.
    3. Exactness. Let v be an exact source and k∈{Int, BigInt, Decimal}, with any numeral dialect. Then for k = Decimal the result is Ok(Decimal(Finite(δ(v)))), unless s.scale = Some(S) and minimal_scale(δ(v)) >S, which gives Err(ScaleExceeded { max: S }), or else s.precision = Some(P) and δ(v) does not fit P, which gives Err(PrecisionExceeded { max: P }); in particular a finite Decimal source is returned unchanged when it is admitted. For k∈{Int, BigInt} the result is Err(ScaleExceeded { max: 0 }) when x(v) is not an integer, else Err(Overflow) when k is Int and x(v)∈/[lo,hi), else Ok(I(x(v))). Every success thus has exactly the numeric value x(v).
    4. Dialect independence. For every v other than Str and Token, coerce_value(v, s) = coerce_value(v, s_0).
    5. Special decimals. If v is a special decimal and k = Decimal, the result is Ok(v), whatever the numeral dialect.
    6. Binary floats. If v = Float(b) is finite and shortest(B64, b) = Some(C), the result is coerce(positional(C), Number, s_0): the value is read through its closest-shortest decimal text C, whose number need not be x(v).
  4. Lemmas. Lemmas 1 to 4 are used by later blocks; Lemma 5 records how each dialect treats canonical lexemes, which coerce_value does not submit to a dialect.
    1. Format values. For each format f, Vf​={0}∪{±n2k:n,k∈Z, 1≤n<2pf​, k≥efmin​−pf​+1, n2k<2efmax​+1}. For q∈Vf​ and every flag z, round_to(f, q, z) = Finite(β) with decode(f, β) = Finite { negative: (q < 0) or (q = 0 and z), value: q }. holds_exactly(f, q) holds exactly when q∈Vf​, and V16​⊂V32​⊂V64​.
    2. Lexemes read back. For every exact source v, parse_non_finite(λ(v)) is None and parse_numeral(λ(v)) is a numeral n with DecimalValue::of_numeral(n) =δ(v); for every finite decimal d, parse_decimal(λ(Decimal(Finite(d)))) = Some(Finite(d)); for every special decimal v, parse_decimal(λ(v)) = Some of the payload of v.
    3. Canonical integers. For an integral numeral n with x=x(of_numeral(n)), integer_of_numeral(n) is the exact integer whose Value::integer is I(x), so that value depends only on x.
    4. Numeric order. For finite decimals a,b, a.cmp_numeric(&b) is the order of x(a) and x(b) in Q.
    5. Dialects on value lexemes. Let k∈{Int, BigInt, Decimal}. For an exact source v, normalize_numeral(λ(v), Number, k, d) is Some(λ(v)) for d∈{Json, ProtoJson, Java, Sql, Toml, Yaml12} and, when v is an Int, also for Yaml11 and Xsd; it is None for Yaml11 and Xsd when v is a BigInt or a finite Decimal. For a special decimal v and k = Decimal, it is Some(λ(v)) when d = Sql and λ(v)∈{NaN, Infinity, -Infinity}, and None for every other pair of dialect and special lexeme (so -NaN is refused under Sql, which names no signed NaN).

The production coerce_value in crates/panproto-inst/src/value/coerce.rs is required to equal this definition exactly on value-admissible specifications, as the named differential tests check.

Outside the domain

  • A float specification with the nearest-keeping-lexeme reading, and an inadmissible specification (L-values-2), are outside this theorem. An inadmissible specification may still produce Some through an earlier null, passthrough, or nonfinite-value branch.
  • An exact source whose digit Nat violates Premise D is outside the proved domain. This is a width boundary on digit_count, separate from Premise A’s allocation boundary.

Definitions used

  • Exact sources are Int(_), BigInt(_) and Decimal(Finite(_)). exact_numeric(v) is their decimal: for Int(i), DecimalValue { negative: i < 0, digits: |i|, exponent: 0 }; for BigInt(β), { β.negative, β.significand, β.zeros }; for Decimal(Finite(d)), d. We write δ(v) for this decimal.
  • A finite decimal d denotes x(d)=(−1)negative⋅D⋅10e with D the number its digits denote and e its exponent. For an exact source x(v)=x(δ(v)) and σ(v) is the negative flag of δ(v); for a finite Float(b), x(v) is the value and σ(v) the sign bit of decode(B64, b).
  • Nat and Int are canonical: a Nat has no most-significant zero limb, its Display writes the decimal numeral of its value with no leading zero ("0" for zero), and Nat::parse reads a nonempty ASCII digit string to its value; Int::new clears the sign of zero, and Int’s Display writes - for a negative value followed by the magnitude.
  • Premise D (digit-width premise) holds when the target pointer width is 32 or 64 bits and every exact-source digit Nat passed to digit_count has N<⌊usize::MAX/9⌋ base-109 limbs. Under this bound, (N - 1) * 9 + top_digits is the exact decimal digit count: the calculation does not overflow usize, and the fallback is not taken. Premise A covers every allocation generated by the calculation.
  • Formats. Format f∈{binary16, binary32, binary64} has precision pf​=11,24,53, exponent width wf​=5,8,11, bias 2wf​−1−1=15,127,1023, efmin​=1−bias and efmax​=bias. decode(f, b) is infinite or NaN for the all-ones exponent field, the subnormal (−1)sF2emin−p+1 for the zero field, and the normal (−1)s(2p−1+F)2E−bias−p+1 otherwise. Vf​ is the set of values q with decode(f, b) = Finite { value: q, .. } for some pattern b.
  • round_to(f, q, z) is the reference rounding: with e=⌊log2​∣q∣⌋ (the result of floor_log2) and qe​=max(e,emin)−p+1, the integer part N of ∣q∣/2qe​ is rounded up when the remainder exceeds 1/2 or equals it with N odd; N=2p renormalizes to 2p−1 with qe​+1; N=0 gives the signed zero; qe​+p−1>emax gives Overflow; otherwise a subnormal pattern for N<2p−1 and a normal one with biased exponent qe​+p−1+bias. A zero q gives Finite of the sign bit when z holds and of 0 otherwise. holds_exactly(f, q) is round_to(f, q, false) being finite and decoding to q.
  • DecimalValue::scaled(lo, hi) gives Value(Rat::zero()) for a zero value; otherwise, with position π=L+e (L the digit count), AtLeastHi when π>hi, BelowLo when π≤lo, and else Value(q) with q=(−1)negativeD⋅ pow10_exact(e); coerce_into_float uses lo=−400, hi=400.
  • pow10_exact(k) returns Rat::pow10(k) (the rational 10k) when k fits i64; otherwise it divides ∣k∣ by 2 with div_rem (quotient h′, remainder r′), computes P = pow10_exact of h=sgn(k)h′, and returns P⋅P⋅10ρ with ρ=0 when r′=0 and ρ=sgn(k) otherwise. For calls reachable from scaled(-400, 400), pow10_exact is exact and structurally representable (step 10). An arbitrary public call may request a power that the dense Nat representation cannot hold.
  • Lexemes. lexeme_of(v, k) is (b.to_string(), Bool) for Bool(b); the i64 decimal of i with class Number for Int(i); "{sign}{significand}e{zeros}" for a BigInt; "{sign}{digits}e{exponent}" for Decimal(Finite(d)); Infinity or -Infinity for an infinite decimal; "{sign}{s}NaN{payload}" (with s for a signalling NaN and the payload omitted when zero) for a NaN decimal, all of class Number; for Float(b), positional(shortest(F, b')) of class Number, with (F,b′) = (binary32, narrow_bits(B32, b)) when k is Float { bits: 32 } and the narrowing exists, and (binary64, b) otherwise, the whole being None when shortest is None; (s, String) for Str(s) and Token(s); (t.to_string(), DateTime) for Temporal(t); ("null", Null) for Null; and None for every other variant. We write λ(v) for the text.
  • Integers. I(x) is Int(x) when −263≤x<263, and otherwise BigInt { negative: x < 0, significand: |x| / 10^z, zeros: z } with z the number of trailing zero digits of ∣x∣. For a fixed-width Int { bits, signed } with B = s.int_bits.unwrap_or(bits) and σ′ = signed && !s.unsigned, [lo,hi) is [−2B−1,2B−1) when σ′ and [0,2B) otherwise (int_range).
  • minimal_scale(d) is 0 for a zero d and otherwise max(0,scale−j) with scale=max(0,−e) and j the number of trailing zero digits of digits. A decimal d fits P when integer_digits(d) ≤P−S (saturating) if s.scale = Some(S), and when positional_digits(d) ≤P otherwise (coerce_decimal).
  • normalize_numeral and its helpers are used through their source text only.

Proof

  1. Branch selection. By the definition of coerce_value: under Any it returns Some(Ok(v)), which is clause 1. Under Float { bits } it applies Format::of_width(bits)?, which is Some for the admissible widths, returns None for the nearest-keeping-lexeme reading (excluded by hypothesis), and otherwise returns Some(coerce_into_float(v, f, s.numeral)), which reads s.numeral only for a Str or Token input (step 11). Under any other kind it returns Some(Err(NonFinite)) for a Float whose binary64 decoding is not finite and for a special decimal when k = BigInt; otherwise it forms s0​ (the struct update ValueSpec { numeral: None, ..*spec }), and returns coerce(λ, c, s) when v is a Str or Token, coerce(λ, c, s_0) for any other v with a lexeme, and Some(Ok(v)) when lexeme_of is None; this is clause 3.1 and 3.2. Clause 3.4 follows: for v neither Str nor Token, the two computations with s and s0​ read s.numeral nowhere (the tests before the lexeme read only k, and both continue with s0​, whose clearing of numeral is idempotent). The calls to coerce are Some because s and s0​ are admissible (L-values-2, Domain clause; admissibility does not involve numeral), so the result is always Some.

  2. Lemma 4.1, finite decodings satisfy the arithmetic condition. Let decode(f, b) be finite with value q=0, fraction F<2p−1 and exponent field E. If E=0, then ∣q∣=F2emin−p+1 with 1≤F<2p−1 and ∣q∣<2emin≤2emax+1. If 0<E<2w−1=2bias+1, then ∣q∣=n2k with n=2p−1+F∈[2p−1,2p) and k=E−bias−p+1≥emin−p+1, and ∣q∣<2p22bias−bias−p+1=2emax+1.

  3. Lemma 4.1, rounding is exact on the condition. Let q satisfy the condition. If q=0, round_to returns Finite of the sign bit exactly when z, which decodes (zero field, zero fraction) to the zero of that sign. Otherwise ∣q∣=n2k as in the condition and e=⌊log2​∣q∣⌋ satisfies 2e≤n2k<2p+k, so k≥e−p+1; with k≥emin−p+1 this gives k≥qe​. Hence ∣q∣/2qe​=n2k−qe​ is an integer N with remainder 0, so no rounding occurs. If e≥emin then N<2e+1/2e−p+1=2p; if e<emin then N<2emin/2emin−p+1=2p−1. So N=2p, N=0, and qe​+p−1=max(e,emin)≤emax because ∣q∣<2emax+1 gives e≤emax. If N<2p−1, then e<emin (for e≥emin gives N≥2e/2e−p+1=2p−1), so qe​=emin−p+1 and the subnormal pattern N decodes to N2emin−p+1=∣q∣. Otherwise the biased exponent max(e,emin)+bias lies in [1,2bias], below the all-ones field, and the pattern decodes to (2p−1+(N−2p−1))2qe​=∣q∣. In both cases the sign bit is set exactly when q<0. This proves the rounding claim, and with step 2 it proves the characterization of Vf​ (a q satisfying the condition is the decoding of the pattern just built).

  4. Lemma 4.1, holds_exactly and inclusions. If q∈Vf​, step 3 with z false gives a finite pattern decoding to q, so holds_exactly(f, q); conversely holds_exactly(f, q) exhibits a pattern decoding to q, so q∈Vf​. The bounds of the condition are monotone in the format: pf​ is 11<24<53, efmin​−pf​+1 is −24>−149>−1074, and efmax​+1 is 16<128<1024. A pair (n,k) meeting the condition for binary16 meets it for binary32, and one for binary32 meets it for binary64, so V16​⊂V32​⊂V64​.

  5. Bounds outside (10−400,10400). If ∣q∣≥10400, then e≥1328 because 21328<10400, so e>emin, qe​=e−p+1, the rounded N is at least 2p−1>0, and qe​+p−1≥e>efmax​ for every f; round_to returns Overflow. If 0<∣q∣<10−400, then e<emin, qe​=emin−p+1≥−1074 and ∣q∣/2qe​<10−40021074<1/2, so N=0 with remainder below 1/2 and round_to returns a signed zero, which is finite and differs from q; by step 4, q∈/Vf​.

  6. Lemma 4.4. cmp_numeric maps each decimal to its sign class (0 when digits is zero, else −1 or 1 by negative), which is the sign of x; when the classes differ or both are 0, comparing the classes is comparing x(a) and x(b). Otherwise both have one nonzero sign, and the result is cmp_magnitude, reversed for negative values. A nonzero decimal with L digits has ∣x∣∈[10π−1,10π) where π=L+e is its position, so different positions order the magnitudes. For equal positions, padding both digit strings on the right with zeros to the common width W gives the numerals of Da​10W−La​=∣x(a)∣10W−π and Db​10W−Lb​=∣x(b)∣10W−π; both strings have W characters and a nonzero first digit, so their lexicographic order is the numeric order of these integers, which is the order of the magnitudes.

  7. Lemma 4.2. For Int(i), λ is - (when i<0) followed by the decimal numeral of ∣i∣ with no leading zero. For BigInt and finite Decimal, λ is - (when negative) followed by the numeral of a Nat, the letter e, and the Display of a Nat or an Int. In each case parse_numeral takes the sign from the first byte, finds the first e (the digit run before it contains none), takes the digit run as integer with an empty fraction and no point, and reads the exponent text with its sign into Int::new, which by canonicity of Int is the exponent written (0 when none). Then of_numeral gives digits = Nat::parse(integer), the original significand, and the stored exponent = written exponent −0, so of_numeral(n) =δ(v). parse_non_finite strips a sign and an optional point and compares the rest with nan, inf, infinity; the rest begins with a digit, so it is None. parse_decimal tries parse_numeral first, hence returns Finite(d) for a finite decimal. For a special decimal, λ contains no e, E or ., so parse_numeral takes the whole text after the sign as its integer part, which is not a digit string, and fails; parse_decimal takes the sign, lowercases the rest, and reads infinity as Infinite { negative }, snan followed by digits as a signalling NaN and nan followed by digits as a quiet NaN with the payload those digits denote (zero when absent). Since λ writes exactly the sign, the s and the nonzero payload of v, the result is v.

  8. Lemma 4.3. For a zero numeral, integer_of_numeral returns Int(0) =I(0). For a nonzero integral one with decimal d of value x, it strips the j trailing zero digits of digits into a count and calls from_parts with significand D/10j and count j+e≥0, whose value is x. from_parts strips any further trailing zeros (none remain), and, when both the count and the significand’s digit count are at most 19, forms the integer and returns Int when it fits i64; otherwise it returns Big with a significand whose last digit is nonzero. If x fits i64 then ∣x∣≤263<1019, so the significand’s digit count plus the count is at most 19 and the Int branch is taken. If x does not fit, the result is Big, whose significand without trailing zeros and count are those of ∣x∣. So Value::integer of the result is I(x).

  9. Integrality and minimal scale. For a nonzero decimal with j trailing zero digits, x=(D/10j)10e+j with D/10j not divisible by 10, so x is an integer exactly when e+j≥0, that is when max(0,−e)−j≤0, that is when minimal_scale is 0. A zero decimal is an integer with minimal scale 0.

  10. Clause 2.1. coerce_into_float on a Float(b) decodes it in binary64; for a finite decoding with value q=x(v) and sign σ(v) it returns Ok(v) when holds_exactly(f, q), which by step 4 is q∈Vf​, and otherwise reject(q, σ(v)), which is Overflow when round_to(f, q, σ(v)) is Overflow and PrecisionExceeded { max: m_f } otherwise (max_significant_digits). On an exact source it computes δ(v).scaled(-400, 400). For AtLeastHi, ∣x(v)∣≥10400 and the result Err(Overflow) agrees with step 5. For BelowLo, 0<∣x(v)∣<10−400, the result Err(PrecisionExceeded { .. }) agrees with step 5, and x(v)∈/Vf​.

    On the Value(q) branch, the exact power is structurally representable across target widths. Let a nonzero decimal have N base-109 digit limbs, digit count L and position π=L+e. This branch has −399≤π≤400. If e≥0, then e≤399. If e<0, then ∣e∣=L−π≤L+399≤9N+399. Hence the dense natural 10∣e∣ requires at most ⌊(9N+399)/9⌋+1≤N+45 limbs. Under Premise D, this bound is below the Vec<u32> structural capacity on both supported pointer widths (on wasm32, N≤477,218,587 and N+45<⌊isize::MAX/4⌋); Premise A supplies the allocation.

    On wasm32 the reachable exponent exceeds usize::MAX by at most 387 and still fits i64; on a 64-bit target at most two halvings make it fit i64. The direct Rat::pow10 path uses pow10_by_halving rather than saturating through usize, and by induction on the nonnegative magnitude it returns 10e: the recursive case squares 10⌊∣e∣/2⌋ and multiplies by 10 exactly when ∣e∣ is odd, placing the power in the denominator when e<0. For a non-i64 Int, pow10_exact uses the signed decomposition e=2h+ρ with ∣h∣<∣e∣ and ρ∈{−1,0,1}, so its result is 10h10h10ρ=10e; division by 2 cannot fail.

    Thus Value(q) has q=x(v). When holds_exactly(f, q) the result is Float of round_to(B64, q, σ(v)), and since q∈Vf​⊂V64​ (step 4), step 3 shows that this pattern decodes in binary64 to q with sign σ(v) (q<0 is σ(v) for q=0); otherwise the result is reject(q, σ(v)) as before.

  11. Clauses 2.2 to 2.4. An infinite Float decoding returns Ok(v). A NaN decoding returns Ok(v) exactly when narrow_bits(f, b) is Some, which by its definition holds exactly when the fraction bits below shift 53−pf​ are zero; the shift is 0 for binary64, where the mask is empty. A special decimal returns Err(NonFinite). For any other value, exact_numeric is None, so the definition uses lexeme_of(v, Float { bits: 64 }) and calls coerce with ValueSpec::of(k) whose numeral is s.numeral filtered to Str and Token inputs. Str(t) and Token(t) give (t,String) and the specification sf​; class String under a float kind makes the dialect relevant, so by L-values-2 row 3 the call returns Err(NotANumber) when normalization fails and otherwise coerce(N, String, ValueSpec::of(k)) (with N=t when there is no dialect), which passes rows 1 to 3 and reaches the float arm, whose class check admits String, giving coerce_float(N, f, Exact); the other values are called with numeral: None: Bool gives class Bool and Temporal class DateTime, both refused by the class check with NotANumber; Null gives class Null and row 1 returns Null; the remaining variants have no lexeme and give Ok(v). The fallback unwrap_or(Err(NotANumber)) is never used, because ValueSpec::of(k) is admissible.

  12. Lemma 4.5. The lexemes of exact sources have three shapes: SI​, an optional - and a digit numeral with no leading zero; SB​, an optional -, a nonzero such numeral, e and a digit numeral; SD​, an optional -, a numeral, e, an optional - and a numeral. None contains +, ., _, :, x, o, b or a letter other than e. The special lexemes begin, after an optional -, with a letter. With k not a float kind and class Number, by dialect:

    • Json and ProtoJson (whose string-and-float case does not apply) call json_number. On SI​, SB​, SD​, decimal_number with the JSON grammar reads the sign, a nonempty integer run with no leading zero (the numerals are minimal), no point, and an exponent with an optional sign and at least one digit, and ends at the last byte; the mantissa neither starts nor ends with . nor starts with -.. So the result is Some(λ). On a special lexeme the integer run and the fraction are empty, so decimal_number is false and the result is None.
    • Java (not a float kind) and Sql call decimal_number with the permissive grammar, which accepts SI​, SB​, SD​ by the same reading and refuses the special lexemes. For Sql with k = Decimal the specials are checked first, on the lowercased text: no finite lexeme lowercases to a listed spelling (they contain no n, a, i or f), NaN, Infinity, -Infinity lowercase to nan, infinity, -infinity and map back to themselves, while -NaN lowercases to -nan, which is unlisted, and a signalling or payload NaN lowercases to snan…, -snan… or nan followed by digits, also unlisted; each unlisted lexeme is then refused by the grammar.
    • Toml: no lexeme is one of the six lowercase specials; an unsigned lexeme does not begin with 0x, 0o or 0b (its second byte is e, a digit, or absent, or its first is a letter), so the prefixed reading is not taken; strip_separators returns the text unchanged since it contains no _; the TOML grammar accepts SI​, SB​, SD​ as JSON does, and the mantissa checks hold, giving Some(λ); a special lexeme fails the grammar, giving None.
    • Yaml12: yaml_special needs a body beginning with ., so it is None; no lexeme begins with 0o or 0x; the permissive grammar accepts the finite shapes and refuses the special ones.
    • Yaml11: yaml_special is None as before; after the sign is removed the body has no 0b, 0x or :. For SI​ the body is 0 or a numeral beginning with a nonzero digit, which the body == "0" or underscored test accepts and returns with its sign, that is Some(λ). For SB​ and SD​ the octal test fails (the body is 0e… or begins with a nonzero digit), the integer test fails on the e, and the float reading splits the mantissa at e and finds no ., returning None. For a special lexeme the same tests fail and the mantissa contains no ., so the result is None.
    • Xsd (not a float kind) requires the grammar without exponent and no e or E: SI​ is accepted unchanged, SB​ and SD​ contain e and are refused, and a special lexeme fails the grammar.

  13. Clause 3.3. The source is not a Str or Token, so by step 1 the result is coerce(λ, Number, s_0), which row 4 of L-values-2 decides since s_0.numeral is None. For k = Decimal, the class check admits Number and coerce_decimal reads parse_decimal(λ) = Finite(δ(v)) (step 7), then applies the scale test and the precision test exactly as stated, returning Decimal(Finite(δ(v))) when both pass. For k = Int or BigInt, coerce_int(λ, w) finds parse_non_finite None, reads the numeral of decimal δ(v) (step 7), refuses with ScaleExceeded { max: 0 } exactly when the minimal scale is positive, that is when x(v) is not an integer (step 9), and for a width compares δ(v) with the decimals of lo and hi by cmp_numeric, which by step 6 is the numeric order, refusing with Overflow exactly when x(v)∈/[lo,hi). It then returns Value::integer(integer_of_numeral(n)) =I(x(v)) by step 8; the call is Some since the minimal scale is 0.

  14. Clauses 3.5 and 3.6. For clause 3.5, k = Decimal, so clause 3.1 does not apply, and the result is coerce(λ(v), Number, s_0); row 4 calls coerce_decimal, which by step 7 parses v back and, v not being finite, applies no test, giving Ok(v). For clause 3.6, k is not Float { bits: 32 }, so lexeme_of uses binary64 and returns (positional(C), Number) when shortest(B64, b) = Some(C), and clause 3.2 gives coerce(positional(C), Number, s_0).

Coercion preserves admitted source lexemes

Statement

Let s be admissible (L-values-2), k = s.kind, and let coerce(t, c, s) = Some(Ok(w)). Let c∗ be the effective class of L-values-2, and let t∘ be the normalized text normalize_numeral(t, c*, k, d) when s.numeral = Some(d) and the dialect is relevant, and t otherwise. Then w retains the following components of the lexeme. Clause 1 covers c = Null; clauses 2 to 9 assume c= Null.

  1. Null. If c = Null, then w = Null.
  2. Strings and tokens. If c= Null and k = Str, then w = Str(t); if k = Token, then w = Token(t).
  3. Temporals. If c= Null and k is Date, Time or DateTime, then w = Temporal(τ) with τ.to_string() =t: the whole lexeme is retained.
  4. Decimals. If c= Null and k = Decimal and parse_numeral(t°) is a numeral n, then w = Decimal(Finite(d)) with d.negative the written minus sign (so -0 keeps its sign), d.digits the number written by the integer and fraction digits of n, and d.exponent the written exponent less the number of fraction digits (so 1.50 and 1.5 give different values). Otherwise w is the special decimal of t∘, with the written sign, the signalling flag (sNaN) and the payload value (the number its digits denote, so NaN05 gives the payload 5) retained.
  5. Integers. If c= Null and k is Int or BigInt, then w=I(x) (L-values-3) where x is the integer the numeral t∘ denotes.
  6. Binary floats. If c= Null, k = Float { bits } with the exact reading, f is its format and mf​ is 5, 9, 17 for binary16, binary32, binary64: a NaN spelling t∘ gives Float(0x7ff8000000000000), or Float(0xfff8000000000000) when written with a minus sign; an infinity spelling gives the binary64 infinity of the written sign; otherwise t∘ is a numeral denoting x, the pattern π = nearest(f, of_numeral(n)) is finite, w = Float(β) where decode(B64, β) equals decode(f, π) (value and sign bit), the sign bit of π is the written minus sign when its value is zero, and either the value of π is x or shortest(f, π) is a decimal denoting x. Conversely, let c∗∈{Number, String}, let the dialect, if relevant, accept t, and let t∘ be neither a NaN nor an infinity spelling. If parse_numeral(t°) is None, the result is Err(NotANumber). Otherwise, with n its numeral, x the value of of_numeral(n) and π = nearest(f, of_numeral(n)), the result is Err(Overflow) when π is Overflow; Ok(Float(widen_bits(f, π))) when π is finite and either its value is x or shortest(f, π) is a decimal denoting x; and Err(PrecisionExceeded { max: m_f }) when π is finite and neither holds. So a finite numeral is accepted exactly when Lf​(x), the value of π, equals x or its closest-shortest text Cf​(Lf​(x)) equals x numerically. (The nearest-keeping-lexeme reading, which accepts every finite numeral, is excluded.)
  7. Booleans. If c= Null and k = Bool, then w = Bool(b) and t equals true (for b true) or false (for b false) up to ASCII case.
  8. Bytes. If c= Null and k = Bytes(e), then w = Bytes(β) and: for Raw, β is the UTF-8 encoding of t; for Latin1, βi​ is the code point of the i-th character of t; for Hex, βi​ is the value of the i-th pair of hexadecimal digits of t, so t is determined by β up to the case of its letters; for the four base64 encodings, t=B=m where the body B is determined by β and the alphabet, and m is (4−∣B∣mod4)mod4 for the padded encodings and either 0 or that number for the others.
  9. Open kind. If k = Any: for c∗ = Number, with t∘ the text after the dialect as above, a NaN or infinity spelling t∘ gives the canonical binary64 pattern of its sign as in clause 6, an integer-form numeral t∘ (no point and no exponent) gives I(x), and any other numeral t∘ of value x gives either Float(β) with shortest(B64, β) denoting x (a zero keeping its written sign) or Decimal(Finite(d)) retaining sign, digits and exponent as in clause 4; for c = DateTime, w = Temporal(τ) with τ.to_string() =t; for c = String, w = Str(t); for c = Bytes, clause 8 with the standard alphabet and optional padding; for c = Bool, clause 7. For c = Tagged(g), the null tag gives Null, a tag naming a scalar kind gives the reading of t under that kind by the clauses above, and any other tag gives the opaque value whose type is g as written and whose field value is Str(t).

Lemma (written temporal forms). For every temporal form F and text x, every element τ of parse_candidates(F, x) satisfies τ.to_string() =x.

The production coerce is required to equal this definition exactly, as the named differential tests check, so it retains the same components.

Outside the domain

  • Refusals keep nothing, and are described in L-values-2. Inadmissible specifications are outside the theorem; the earlier null and dialect branches described there may still produce an outcome.
  • The float nearest-keeping-lexeme reading is not lossless by design: its value is the nearest pattern and its lexeme is kept outside the value. It is excluded from clause 6.

Definitions used

  • The rows of coerce and the effective class are those of L-values-2; I(x), Vf​ and Lemma 4.1 are those of L-values-3.
  • parse_candidates(F, x) returns, for x = infinity or -infinity, the infinite temporal of form F with a local offset (none for a time form), and otherwise every split x=b⋅o (at a character boundary, in order of decreasing ∣b∣) for which the body reader of F accepts b and parse_offset accepts o; the date-time body reader splits b at the first T, t or space into a date body, the separator and a time body. parse(F, x) is the first candidate, and parse_any(x) the single distinct candidate over the three forms, when there is exactly one.
  • parse_date_body, parse_year, parse_time_body, parse_seconds, parse_offset and digits_n are the reference readers; digits_n(s, n) accepts exactly a string of n ASCII digits and returns its value. write_date, write_time and the Display of Offset and Temporal are the reference writers.
  • coerce_temporal, coerce_decimal, coerce_int, coerce_float, coerce_bool, coerce_any, decode_bytes and decode_base64 are the reference readers called by coerce; nearest(f, d) is round_to(f, q, d.negative) on the exact value q of d (computed by scaled with pow10_exact, exact for every exponent, L-values-3 step 10) when d is zero or its position lies in (−400,400], Overflow above, and the zero of sign d.negative below. The base64 encodings are read by crate::bytes::decode_base64(text, padded), the URL-safe ones after refusing a text that contains + or / and translating - to + and _ to /; Latin1 by crate::bytes::latin1_encode.

Proof

  1. Reduction. By L-values-2, a call with c = Null is decided by row 1, which returns Null under every kind; this is clause 1, and it is why clauses 2 to 9 assume c= Null. For c= Null, a successful call is decided by row 2 (for k= Any a call with class String, so c∗ = String, which is not Null; for k = Any the tag reading), and otherwise by row 4 applied to t∘ (row 3 replacing t by the normalized text when the dialect is relevant) with the kind and parameters of s; in no case does row 1 apply again. The cases below follow the arms of row 4.
  2. Lemma, offsets. Let parse_offset(o) =ω. For o empty, Z or z the result is Local, Zulu(Upper) or Zulu(Lower), which display as the empty string, Z and z. Otherwise o is a sign followed by a body cut at : into pieces. With three pieces h,m,r of two digits (h≤23, m,r≤59): if r=0 the result is NegZero(ExtendedSeconds) when 60h+m=0 and the sign is -, displaying -00:00:00 =o, and otherwise Fixed(±(60h + m), ExtendedSeconds), displaying the sign of the stored value (- exactly when the sign was - and 60h+m>0, + otherwise, which is the written sign since a written - with zero gave NegZero), then ⌊(60h+m)/60⌋=h and (60h+m)mod60=m in two digits and :00. If r>0 the result is FixedSeconds(±(3600h + 60m + r)), displaying the written sign and h, m, r recovered by division since 60m+r<3600. With two pieces the same argument applies to Extended (-00:00 or the sign, h, :, m). With any other number of pieces (one, or four or more), the form is Basic when the body has four bytes and HourOnly otherwise. Basic reads body.get(..2) and body.get(2..), which exist only when byte 2 is a character boundary, and requires each to be two digits, so a body containing : is refused there; the result displays as sign, h, m without a colon. HourOnly requires the whole body to be two digits, so again a : is refused; the result displays as sign and h, the minutes being zero; each displays the sign and the digits written. In every case the display is o, because a two-digit string of value v is the two-digit zero-padded numeral of v.
  3. Lemma, dates. Let parse_date_body(b) =Δ. If b begins with ---, the rest is two digits (the day), displayed --- and the day in two digits. If b begins with -- (and not ---), the rest is a month and a day separated by - or a month alone, displayed --m-d or --m. Otherwise b is an optional -, a year body y and up to two --separated two-digit fields (a third - would put a - inside the day field, which digits_n refuses). parse_year records the value, the width ∣y∣ and negative_zero for -0000. The writer prints - exactly when the value is negative or negative_zero holds, which is exactly when a - was written, then the magnitude zero-padded to the width; the numeral of the magnitude has at most ∣y∣ digits, so the padded numeral is a digit string of length ∣y∣ denoting the same value as y, and two digit strings of one length denoting one value are equal. It then prints -m and -d for the fields present. valid_date filters without changing fields. So the display is b.
  4. Lemma, times. Let parse_time_body(b) =T. For -- followed by seconds, parse_seconds reads two digits and, when a . follows, a nonempty digit fraction; the writer’s arm (no hour, no minute, a second) prints --, the two digits and . with the fraction when it is nonempty, which is exactly when a . was written. For - followed by m:sec or m the arms (no hour, minute and second) and (no hour, minute only) print the same. Otherwise b is cut by : into at most three pieces: an hour, an optional minute and optional seconds (digits_n refuses a further :), and the arms (hour only), (hour, minute) and (hour, minute, second) print exactly the pieces present, the arm (hour, no minute, second) not arising. The range checks change no field. So the display is b.
  5. Lemma, conclusion. The infinite candidates display infinity or -infinity, which is x. A date candidate displays its date body then its offset, which by steps 3 and 2 is b⋅o=x; a time candidate likewise by steps 4 and 2. A date-time candidate whose body b was cut at index a displays its date, which is b[..a] by step 3, the separator character recorded from b[a], its time, which is b[a+1..] by step 4, and its offset, which is o by step 2; the display is b⋅o=x.
  6. Clauses 2 and 3. For Str and Token, row 4 returns Str(t) or Token(t) for every class it accepts; c∗ is not Number there and the kind is not numeric, so the dialect is not relevant and t∘=t. For a temporal kind, coerce_temporal returns Temporal(parse(F, t)) (when the offset checks pass), the first candidate of parse_candidates(F, t), and the Lemma gives τ.to_string() =t.
  7. Clause 4. coerce_decimal returns Decimal of parse_decimal(t°), whose finite branch is of_numeral(parse_numeral(t°)), with negative the written sign, digits = Nat::parse(integer ++ fraction) and exponent the written exponent less fraction.len(); the scale and precision tests only refuse. Its special branch takes the written sign, snan or nan and the payload digits.
  8. Clause 5. coerce_int returns Value::integer(integer_of_numeral(n)) for the numeral n of t∘, which by L-values-3 Lemma 4.3 is I(x).
  9. Clause 6. coerce_float returns, for a NaN or infinity spelling recognized by parse_non_finite, the binary64 patterns nan_bits(negative) and inf_bits(negative), which are the stated constants. Otherwise it reads the numeral, takes π = nearest(f, d), refuses an overflow, and accepts only when shortest(f, π) denotes x (dec_equals) or the exact value of d equals the value of π (denotes_exactly), returning Float(widen_bits(f, π)). For a finite π with value y and sign bit z, widen_bits is round_to(B64, y, z), and since y∈Vf​⊂V64​, L-values-3 Lemma 4.1 shows that it decodes in binary64 to y with sign bit z. A zero π arises in three ways: from round_to(f, 0, d.negative) for a zero d, which takes the sign d.negative; from the below-range branch of nearest, which takes the sign d.negative; and from round_to(f, q, d.negative) on a nonzero in-range q whose rounded significand is 0 (for instance 1e-30 under binary16), which takes the sign of q, and that sign is d.negative because d is nonzero. In every case the sign bit is the written sign. (In the last two cases π does not denote the nonzero x, and shortest(f, π) is a zero, so the lexeme is refused; the clause holds a fortiori.) For the converse, let c∗∈{Number, String}, so the class check of the float arm passes, and let t∘ be neither a NaN nor an infinity spelling, so parse_non_finite(t°) is None. coerce_float then returns Err(NotANumber) when parse_numeral(t°) is None; under the exact reading it returns Err(Overflow) when nearest(f, d) is Overflow, and for a finite pattern π it returns Ok(Float(widen_bits(f, π))) when canonical || denotes_exactly and Err(PrecisionExceeded { max }) otherwise, with max = max_significant_digits(f) =mf​. It remains to identify the two tests. canonical is shortest(f, π) being Some(C) with dec_equals(C, d), that is C.cmp_numeric(d) being Equal for the decimal of C, which by L-values-3 Lemma 4.4 holds exactly when C denotes x. denotes_exactly(f, d, π) holds exactly when d.scaled(-400, 400) is Value(q) and decode(f, π) is finite with value q. If d is zero or its position lies in (−400,400], scaled gives q=x exactly (L-values-3 step 10), so the test is value(π)=x. If the position exceeds 400, nearest is Overflow and the test is not reached. If the position is at most −400, scaled gives BelowLo and the test is false, while π is a zero and x=0, so value(π)=x is false as well. Hence canonical || denotes_exactly is exactly the stated condition.
  10. Clauses 7 and 8. coerce_bool accepts exactly true and false up to ASCII case. For bytes: Raw returns t.as_bytes(); Latin1 maps each character to its code point and refuses one above 0xFF; Hex requires an even length and maps each pair of hexadecimal digits to 16h+l. For base64, a URL-safe text containing + or / is refused and the others are translated by the bijection - to +, _ to / between the two alphabets (on texts without + and /), so it suffices to treat the standard alphabet. bytes::optional splits the text at its first = into B and a padding that must be one or two = or empty, requires every byte of B to be in the alphabet, computes ν=(4−∣B∣mod4)mod4, refuses ν>2 (that is ∣B∣mod4=1) and a nonempty padding of length other than ν, and returns B followed by ν =; decode_base64 with padding required additionally refuses a text different from that result, so the padding is ν there and 0 or ν otherwise. It then decodes each four-character quantum to three bytes, the last quantum to one byte when it ends in two = (requiring the low four bits of its second sextet to be zero) and to two bytes when it ends in one = (requiring the low two bits of its third sextet to be zero). So β is the bit string of the sextets of B cut into whole bytes, with the leftover bits zero. Writing ∣B∣=4q+r with r∈{0,2,3} gives ∣β∣=⌊6∣B∣/8⌋=3q+0,3q+1,3q+2, so ∣B∣ is determined by ∣β∣; the bit string of B is then the bits of β followed by 6∣B∣−8∣β∣ zero bits, and each character of B is the alphabet entry of its six bits. So B is determined by β.
  11. Clause 9. coerce_any on class Number (after the dialect, by row 3) returns the patterns of step 9 for a non-finite spelling; for an integer-form numeral the minimal scale is 0, so integer_of_numeral is Some and gives I(x) by Lemma 4.3 of L-values-3; otherwise it rounds to binary64 by nearest and returns Float(β) exactly when β is finite and shortest(B64, β) denotes x, a zero β taking the written sign as in step 9, and Decimal(Finite(of_numeral(n))) otherwise, retaining as in step 7. On class DateTime it returns parse(Date, t) or else parse_any(t), each a candidate of some form for t, so the Lemma applies. On String it returns Str(t), on Bytes it calls decode_bytes(t, Base64) (step 10), and on Bool it calls coerce_bool. A tagged lexeme under Any is read by coerce_tagged_open, which returns Null for the null tag, reads t under the tag’s kind with the clauses above, or returns the opaque value whose type is g as written and whose field value is Str(t).

Coercion is idempotent

Statement

Let s be value-admissible (L-values-3) with kind k, and let s0​ be s with numeral set to None. Let Img(s) be the set of values w with coerce(t, c, s) = Some(Ok(w)) for some text t and class c.

  1. Dialects add no results. Img(s)⊂Img(s0​).
  2. Direct results are fixed. For every w∈Img(s0​), coerce_value(w, s) = Some(Ok(w)).
  3. Idempotence. For every value v with coerce_value(v, s) = Some(Ok(w)), coerce_value(w, s) = Some(Ok(w)). This holds for every kind and every numeral dialect.

The production coerce_value is required to equal this definition exactly, as the named differential tests check, so the same holds of it.

Outside the domain

Specifications that are not value-admissible (an inadmissible kind, or a float kind with the nearest-keeping-lexeme reading) are outside this law (L-values-3). Some inadmissible specifications still admit null or passthrough values. No other input is excluded.

Definitions used

  • coerce, its rows, its Domain clause and its parameter dependence, as in L-values-2; a numeral dialect is relevant for (c,k) when c = Number, or c = String and k is Int, BigInt, Float or Decimal.
  • coerce_value, lexeme_of, I(x), Vf​, and the clauses and Lemmas of L-values-3; in particular clause 2.4 (under a float kind a Str or Token is read with the dialect of s and every other value without one) and clause 3.2: a Str or Token is read under s, and every other value with a lexeme under s0​.
  • The written-form Lemma of L-values-4: every candidate of parse_candidates(F, x) displays as x.

Proof

  1. Clause 1. Let coerce(t, c, s) = Some(Ok(w)), and follow the rows of L-values-2. Row 1 gives Null, which coerce(t, Null, s₀) also gives. Row 2 under Any reads only the tag and calls coerce with ValueSpec::of(k'), so the same call is made under s0​; row 2 under a declared kind is a call with class String, treated next. If the dialect is relevant and s.numeral is Some, row 3 returns coerce(N, c, s₀), so w∈Img(s0​). Otherwise either s.numeral is None, so s=s0​, or the dialect is not relevant, and then s and s0​ have the same kind and parameters and the parameter-dependence clause of L-values-2 gives coerce(t, c, s) = coerce(t, c, s₀).
  2. Clause 2, kinds Any and Float. Under Any, coerce_value(w, s) is Ok(w) for every w. Under Float { bits } with format f, the successes of coerce under s0​ are Null, the binary64 NaNs 0x7ff8000000000000 and 0xfff8000000000000, the binary64 infinities, and Float(widen_bits(f, π)) for finite π (L-values-4 clause 6). coerce_value(·, s) is coerce_into_float(·, f, s.numeral), which reads s through f and, for a Str or Token input only, through s.numeral; none of the values listed is a Str or Token, so for them it reads s only through f. On Null it finds no exact value and the lexeme ("null", Null), and row 1 returns Null. On the two NaNs the fraction field is 251, whose bits below 53−pf​≤42 are zero, so narrow_bits is Some and the value is kept. On an infinity it keeps the value. On Float(widen_bits(f, π)) the binary64 value lies in Vf​ (L-values-4 clause 6), so holds_exactly(f, ·) holds by L-values-3 Lemma 4.1 and the value is kept.
  3. Clause 2, kinds Bool, Str, Token, Bytes. The successes under s0​ are Null, and respectively Bool(b), Str(t), Token(t) and Bytes(β). Null is not a Str or Token, so it is read under s0​, where row 1 returns it. Bool(b) is read under s0​ from (b.to_string(), Bool), and coerce_bool reads true or false back as b. Str(t) and Token(t) are read under s from (t, String); the kind is not numeric, so the dialect is not relevant and row 4 returns Str(t) or Token(t). Bytes(β) has no lexeme and is neither a non-finite float nor a special decimal, so coerce_value returns Ok(Bytes(β)).
  4. Clause 2, temporal kinds. A success is Null (fixed as in step 3) or Temporal(τ) with τ = parse(F, t), the first candidate of parse_candidates(F, t) for the form F of k, whose offset passed the checks of coerce_temporal. It is read under s0​ from (τ.to_string(), DateTime), which is (t,DateTime) by the Lemma of L-values-4; row 4 calls coerce_temporal(t, s₀), which computes the same τ and applies the same offset checks (with_time_zone is the same in s and s0​), returning Ok(Temporal(τ)).
  5. Clause 2, kinds Int and BigInt. A success is Null (fixed) or I(x) for an integer x that the call found within [lo,hi) when k is a fixed-width Int. I(x) is an exact source of value x, and by L-values-3 clause 3.3, which holds with any numeral dialect, coerce_value(I(x), s) is Ok(I(x)).
  6. Clause 2, kind Decimal. A success is Null (fixed) or a decimal. A finite Decimal(Finite(d)) was admitted by coerce_decimal, whose scale and precision tests depend only on d and on parameters shared by s and s0​, so L-values-3 clause 3.3 returns Ok(Decimal(Finite(d))). A special decimal is returned unchanged by L-values-3 clause 3.5.
  7. Clause 3. Let coerce_value(v, s) = Some(Ok(w)). Under Any, w=v and step 2 applies. Under a float kind, by L-values-3 clause 2 either w=v was kept because it is a finite Float with value in Vf​, an infinity, a NaN with narrowable fraction, or a value without a lexeme, and the same test keeps it again; or w = Float(β) from an exact source with x∈Vf​, whose binary64 value is x (L-values-3 clause 2.1), so holds_exactly(f, x) keeps it; or w is Null, fixed by step 2; or v is a Str or Token and w = coerce(t, String, s_f) with sf​ = ValueSpec::of(k) carrying s.numeral (L-values-3 clause 2.4). The specification sf​ is value-admissible and its dialect-free form is ValueSpec::of(k), so clause 1 gives w∈Img(sf​)⊂Img(ValueSpec::of(k)), and step 2 applied to ValueSpec::of(k) shows that coerce_value(w, ValueSpec::of(k)) is Ok(w). That w is a Float (a dialect turns the string into a number before coerce_float reads it), not a Str or Token, so coerce_into_float reads it without any dialect and depends only on f; hence coerce_value(w, s) = coerce_value(w, ValueSpec::of(k)) = Ok(w). Under any other kind, by L-values-3 clause 3.2 either lexeme_of(v, k) is None and w=v, which passes the same tests again and still has no lexeme, so coerce_value(w, s) = Ok(w); or w is coerce(λ, c, s) (for a Str or Token v), which lies in Img(s)⊂Img(s0​) by clause 1, or coerce(λ, c, s₀) ∈Img(s0​). In both cases clause 2 gives coerce_value(w, s) = Ok(w).

Direct and value coercion have the same fixed points

Statement

Let s be value-admissible (L-values-3) with kind k, let s0​ be s with numeral set to None, let Img be as in L-values-5, let Fix(s) be the set of values w with coerce_value(w, s) = Some(Ok(w)), and let NoLex(s) be the set of values w with lexeme_of(w, k) = None that are not non-finite Floats.

  1. Direct results are fixed points. Img(s)⊂Img(s0​)⊂Fix(s).
  2. Declared non-float kinds. If k is neither Any nor a float kind, then Fix(s)=Img(s0​)∪NoLex(s), and every w∈Fix(s) with lexeme_of(w, k) = Some((λ, c)) is the direct coercion of its own lexeme: coerce(λ, c, s₀) = Some(Ok(w)). So direct coercion and value coercion have the same fixed points, apart from the values without a lexeme, which value coercion keeps and direct coercion cannot produce from a lexeme of theirs.
  3. Open kind. If k = Any, Fix(s) is the set of all values.
  4. Float kinds. If k = Float { bits } with format f, then Fix(s) is the union of the finite Floats whose binary64 value lies in Vf​, the infinite Floats, the NaN Floats whose fraction bits below 53−pf​ are zero, Null, and the values of the variants Bytes, CidLink, Blob, Opaque, Unknown, List and LabeledNull.

The production coerce and coerce_value are required to equal these definitions exactly, as the named differential tests check, so the same fixed-point sets describe them.

Outside the domain

The fixed-point characterization is limited to value-admissible specifications (L-values-3). An excluded specification may still have fixed points, including Null under an inadmissible integer kind. No other input is excluded.

Definitions used

  • coerce, its rows and the relevance of a numeral dialect, as in L-values-2.
  • coerce_value, lexeme_of, Vf​, pf​, and the clauses of L-values-3, in particular clause 2.4 (under a float kind a Str or Token is read with the dialect of s and every other value without one) and clause 3.2: a Str or Token is read under s, and every other value with a lexeme under s0​.
  • Img and clauses 1 and 2 of L-values-5.
  • lexeme_of(w, k) is None exactly for the variants Bytes, CidLink, Blob, Opaque, Unknown, List, LabeledNull, and for a Float on which shortest returns None; every BigInt and every Decimal has a lexeme.

Proof

  1. Clause 1 is clauses 1 and 2 of L-values-5.
  2. Clause 2, inclusion from left to right. Let w∈Fix(s) with k neither Any nor a float kind. By L-values-3 clause 3.1, w is not a non-finite Float. If lexeme_of(w, k) is None, then w∈NoLex(s). Otherwise, by L-values-3 clause 3.2, coerce_value(w, s) is coerce(λ, c, s₀) when w is not a Str or Token, which thus equals Some(Ok(w)). When w is a Str or Token, coerce_value(w, s) is coerce(λ, String, s). If k is Int, BigInt or Decimal, the dialect (if any) is relevant for class String, and by L-values-2 rows 3 and 4 that call returns a refusal, Null, an integer or a decimal, never a Str or Token, contradicting w∈Fix(s); so k is not numeric, the dialect is not relevant, and the parameter dependence of L-values-2 gives coerce(λ, String, s) = coerce(λ, String, s₀). In both cases coerce(λ, c, s₀) = Some(Ok(w)), which is the second sentence of clause 2 and places w in Img(s0​).
  3. Clause 2, inclusion from right to left. Img(s0​)⊂Fix(s) by clause 1. Let w∈NoLex(s). It is not a non-finite Float by definition, and not a special decimal, because every decimal has a lexeme; so L-values-3 clause 3.1 does not refuse it, and clause 3.2 returns Ok(w) because its lexeme is None.
  4. Clause 3: under Any, coerce_value(w, s) is Some(Ok(w)) for every w (L-values-3 clause 1).
  5. Clause 4, by the cases of L-values-3 clause 2. A finite Float is returned unchanged exactly when its value lies in Vf​, and refused otherwise (clause 2.1). An infinite Float is returned unchanged; a NaN Float exactly when its low fraction bits vanish, and is refused otherwise (clause 2.2). A special decimal is refused (clause 2.3). An exact source gives either a refusal or a Float, a different variant, so it is not fixed (clause 2.1). Str(t) and Token(t) give, with or without the dialect of s, the result of coerce_float on the possibly normalized text or the refusal NotANumber, so a Float or a refusal, never the original variant; Bool and Temporal are refused; Null gives Null; and the seven listed variants are returned unchanged (clause 2.4). This is the stated set, and it contains Img(s) by clause 1.
