Canonical value bytes are injective

Statement

Under Assumption W of L-values-10, let D be the encoder’s domain, the set of values v: Value with value_bytes(&v) not None. Then:

  1. (domain) v∈D exactly when every temporal component of v satisfies Temporal::well_formed;
  2. (injectivity) for all v,w∈D, value_bytes(&v) == value_bytes(&w) implies v=w under the derived == of Value;
  3. (left inverse) for every v∈D whose big-integer components are canonical, decode_value(&value_bytes(&v).unwrap()) is Some(v);
  4. (consequence) for all v,w∈D, representation(&v, &w) is Some(v == w).

Property 2 covers every value of D, including a Value::BigInt whose fields are not canonical. The production canonical encoder of Value named on the block’s File line is required to equal value_bytes exactly.

Outside the domain

A target that violates Assumption W’s pointer-width condition, or a held value that violates its limb bound, is outside the proved domain. A value with an ill-formed temporal component is outside D: write_temporal returns None, so value_bytes returns None and no bytes exist to compare; representation then returns None, which expression evaluation reports as EvalError::UndefinedRepresentation. A value of D with a noncanonical big-integer component (for instance BigIntValue { negative: false, significand: 5, zeros: 0 }, which lies within i64, or a significand ending in 0) has bytes and satisfies property 2, but read_bigint refuses those bytes, so decode_value returns None on them; property 3 is stated for canonical big integers only.

Definitions used

  • Byte strings are finite sequences of bytes, ⋅ is concatenation and ϵ the empty string. E(v) abbreviates the bytes write_value appends for v, so value_bytes(&v) is Some(E(v)) for v∈D.
  • An encoder E is prefix-determining on a set S when for all x,x′∈S and byte strings s,s′, E(x)⋅s=E(x′)⋅s′ implies x=x′ and s=s′. Taking s=s′=ϵ shows that a prefix-determining encoder is injective.
  • Writer primitives: tag(t) is the one byte t; u32, u64 and i64 append to_le_bytes, the 4 or 8 little-endian bytes of the value, a bijection between the integer type and byte arrays of that length; len(n) is u64(n), where u64::try_from(n) succeeds under Assumption W, so the fallback is never taken; raw(b) is len(|b|) followed by b; str(s) is raw of the UTF-8 bytes of s; write_digits(n) is str(n.to_string()).
  • Assumption W of L-values-10: the target’s pointer width is at most 64 bits, so u64::try_from of a usize succeeds and is injective, and usize::try_from of a u64 that came from a usize succeeds with that usize.
  • Facts N1 to N3 on Nat and Int are those of L-values-10: Nat and Int hold canonical representations, n.to_string() is the decimal numeral of n with no leading zero ("0" for zero), and an Int is the pair of its sign flag and magnitude, the flag set only on a nonzero magnitude.
  • write_value writes a variant tag (0 Bool, 1 Int, 2 Float, 3 Str, 4 Bytes, 5 CidLink, 6 Blob, 7 Token, 8 Null, 9 Opaque, 10 Unknown, 11 List, 12 LabeledNull, 13 Decimal, 14 BigInt, 15 Temporal) followed by the payload written in its arm; a map is len of its entry count and then, in the map’s ascending key order, str(key) and the value’s encoding.
  • The components of a value are the value itself and, recursively, the items of a List and the field values of an Opaque or Unknown map. A temporal component is a component of variant Temporal, and a big-integer component one of variant BigInt.
  • A BigIntValue is canonical when its significand is nonzero, its last digit (digit(0)) is nonzero, and ExactInteger::from_parts of its fields returns Big; these are exactly the checks of read_bigint.
  • For a temporal t: form(), well_formed(), is_complete() and Temporal::infinite as defined in the reference temporal module; complete_layout(t) holds when t is finite, complete, has a year written without a negative zero and with the canonical width max(4,digits of ∣y∣), has offset Local, Zulu(Upper), Zulu(Lower), Fixed(_, Extended) or NegZero(Extended), and is Local when it is a date without a time.

Proof

  1. Primitive codes are prefix-determining. A code of fixed length k that is injective (tag on bytes, u8::from on booleans, u32, u64, i64) is prefix-determining: the first k bytes of E(x)⋅s=E(x′)⋅s′ give E(x)=E(x′), hence x=x′, and the remaining bytes give s=s′. raw is prefix-determining on byte strings: the first 8 bytes give ∣b∣=∣b′∣=n, the next n bytes give b=b′, and the rest gives s=s′. str is then prefix-determining because a String is determined by its bytes, and write_digits because, by N1 and N2, two Nats with the same numeral denote the same number and are equal.
  2. Sequencing. If E1​ is prefix-determining on S1​ and, for each x∈S1​, E2x​ is prefix-determining on S2​(x), then (x,y)↦E1​(x)⋅E2x​(y) is prefix-determining: from E1​(x)⋅(E2x​(y)⋅s)=E1​(x′)⋅(E2x′​(y′)⋅s′) we get x=x′ and E2x​(y)⋅s=E2x​(y′)⋅s′, hence y=y′ and s=s′. By induction on the number of fields, a writer that emits a finite sequence of prefix-determining fields, where which fields follow may depend on fields already written, is prefix-determining on any set on which the written fields determine the value. A leading tag byte whose value selects the remaining fields is the special case of a first field.
  3. Property 1. Every arm of write_value returns Some except through ? on write_map, on a list item, or on write_temporal. write_temporal(t) returns None when t is not well formed. When t is well formed it returns Some: the complete-layout branch fails only at the FixedSeconds arm, which complete_layout excludes; the infinity branch fails only for the form Time, which well_formed excludes for an infinity; and t.form() is not None for a well-formed finite t, since well_formed returns false in that case. Induction over components gives property 1, and every component of a value of D lies in D.
  4. Decimal payloads. write_decimal is prefix-determining on all of Decimal. Its first byte is u8::from(negative) ∈{0,1} for a finite value, 2 for an infinity and 3 for a NaN, so equal first bytes give the same variant and, for a finite value, the same sign flag. A finite value then writes write_digits(digits), the exponent’s sign byte and write_digits of its magnitude; by N3 an Int is the pair of those two fields, and a DecimalValue is the triple of flag, digits and exponent. An infinity writes its sign byte; a NaN writes its sign and signalling bytes and write_digits(payload). Steps 1 and 2 conclude.
  5. Big-integer payloads. write_bigint writes the sign byte, write_digits(significand) and write_digits(zeros), and a BigIntValue is the triple of those fields, so it is prefix-determining on every BigIntValue, canonical or not, by steps 1 and 2.
  6. Temporals in the complete layout. Let t be well formed with complete_layout(t). Its first byte is 0, 1 or 2 as t has a date only, a time only, or both (is_complete excludes neither), and its infinity is None. If a date is present, it writes the year value as i64 and month and day bytes; complete_layout makes year, month and day present, the year’s negative_zero false and its width the canonical width of its value, so the three written numbers determine the date. A separator byte (T, t or space, three distinct bytes) is written exactly when the separator is present, which by well_formed is exactly when both parts are, a fact fixed by the first byte. If a time is present, it writes hour, minute and second bytes, which is_complete makes present, and str(fraction). With a time present, the offset is written as 0 for Local, 1 then Z or z for Zulu(Upper) or Zulu(Lower), 2 then i64::from(m) for Fixed(m, _), and 3 for NegZero(_); complete_layout admits no other offset and fixes the form of Fixed and NegZero as Extended, and i64::from is injective on i16. Without a time (first byte 0), complete_layout makes the offset Local. So the written fields determine t, and by steps 1 and 2 the writer is prefix-determining on this layout.
  7. Temporals in the extended layout. Let t be well formed with complete_layout(t) false. If t is infinite, it writes 6 for the form Date or 7 for DateTime (well_formed excludes Time), a sign byte (0 negative, 1 positive), and write_offset_form: a variant byte 0 to 4, then the Zulu case byte 0, 1 or 2, or i64::from(minutes) and the injective offset_form_tag of the five forms, or that tag alone for NegZero, or i64::from(seconds) from i32. well_formed makes date, time and separator None, so form, sign and offset determine t. If t is finite, its first byte 3, 4 or 5 is t.form(), which for a finite value fixes which of date and time are present; then write_date_form writes a presence byte for the year and, if present, its value as i64, its negative_zero byte and its width as u64 (injective on usize under Assumption W), followed by presence bytes and values for month and day; the separator byte follows exactly when the form is DateTime (well_formed); write_time_form writes presence bytes and values for hour, minute and second and str(fraction); and write_offset_form the offset. Every field of t is written or fixed by an earlier field, so by steps 1 and 2 the writer is prefix-determining on this layout.
  8. The first bytes of the two layouts lie in {0,1,2} and {3,…,7} respectively, so by step 2 (a leading byte selecting the layout), write_temporal is prefix-determining on all well-formed temporals.
  9. We prove by structural induction on v∈D that for every w∈D and byte strings s,s′, E(v)⋅s=E(w)⋅s′ implies v=w and s=s′. The first byte is the variant tag, one per variant, so w has the variant of v. The cases: Bool (one byte, u8::from), Int (i64), Float (u64 of the bits), LabeledNull (u64), Str, CidLink and Token (str), Bytes (raw), Blob (str, str, u64), Null (no payload), Decimal (step 4), BigInt (step 5) and Temporal (step 8, both temporals well formed by property 1); each is prefix-determining by steps 1 and 2. List: equal counts give one length n, and applying the induction hypothesis to the n items in order (each a component of v, hence in D) gives equal items and equal suffixes. Unknown, and Opaque after its str(type_): equal counts, then for each entry in order str(key) by step 1 and the value by the induction hypothesis, so the two maps have the same ascending sequence of entries; a BTreeMap is determined by that sequence, so the maps are equal.
  10. Property 2 is step 9 with s=s′=ϵ.
  11. Readers invert the primitive writers. On input E(x)⋅s, each reader returns x and leaves the cursor at s: tag returns the byte; u32, u64, i64 apply from_le_bytes, the inverse of to_le_bytes; count returns the u64 as usize, which succeeds for a length that came from a usize (Assumption W); raw reads the count and takes that many bytes; str applies String::from_utf8 to the bytes of a String, which succeeds with that string; read_bool maps 0 and 1 back. read_digits on write_digits(n) reads n.to_string(), which has no leading zero unless it is "0" (N2), so its check passes, and Nat::parse splits the numeral into nine-digit chunks from the right, exactly the limbs Display wrote (the top one unpadded), and normalizes, so it returns n (N1).
  12. Readers invert the compound payloads. read_decimal reads the first byte and, for 0 or 1, the digits, the exponent’s sign and magnitude; the check en && mag.is_zero() fails because by N3 a set sign flag has a nonzero magnitude, and Int::new(en, mag) returns the exponent unchanged; bytes 2 and 3 read back an infinity and a NaN field by field. For a canonical big integer, read_bigint reads its three fields and its checks pass by the definition of canonical. For a temporal in the complete layout, read_temporal reads the date as Year { value, negative_zero: false, width } with the canonical width and present month and day, which equals t’s date by step 6; read_time returns present hour, minute and second and the fraction, whose digit check passes because well_formed makes a nonempty fraction all digits; read_offset returns Local, Zulu(Upper), Zulu(Lower), Fixed(m, Extended) (in both branches of m == 0, with i16::try_from succeeding on a value that came from i16) or NegZero(Extended), which is t’s offset by step 6; tag 0 sets offset Local and tags 0 and 1 separator None, as step 6 requires. For the extended layout, tags 3 to 5 read each field with the inverse of its writer (presence bytes, i64, u64 and the narrowing conversions, which succeed on values that came from i16, i32 and usize), and tags 6 and 7 read the sign and offset and build Temporal::infinite, which for a form other than Time returns no date, time or separator, as t has by step 7. In every case the rebuilt value equals t, so the final well_formed check passes.
  13. Property 3 by structural induction: read_value on E(v)⋅s returns v and leaves the cursor at s. The tag selects the arm of v’s variant; scalar payloads by step 11; Decimal, BigInt (canonical by hypothesis) and Temporal by step 12; List by the count and the induction hypothesis on items. For a map, write_map wrote the keys in strictly ascending order (a BTreeMap iterates its distinct keys in ascending String order), so the check last >= k in read_map, which uses the same order, never fires, and inserting the entries rebuilds the map. With s=ϵ the reader ends at the last byte, so done() holds and decode_value returns Some(v).
  14. Property 4. For v,w∈D, representation(&v, &w) is Some(E(v) == E(w)) by its definition, and E(v)=E(w) exactly when v=w: one direction is property 2, the other holds because value_bytes is a function.

Expression evaluation is exact and lexically scoped

Statement

Expression evaluation eval(e, ρ) is lexically scoped, treats builtins as curried functions, performs exact operations on exact values, evaluates in a stated order, and reports every failure as a typed EvalError. The domain is every expression e: Expr and every environment ρ: BTreeMap<String, Value>. Internally, eval lifts ρ to the runtime environment binding each name to Runtime::Value of its value and evaluates with eval_runtime, whose environments bind names to runtimes: values, closures and partial builtins. We write k= arity(op) for the arity of a builtin.

  1. (variables) eval_runtime(&Variable(x), σ) is Ok(σ(x)) when x is bound in σ; otherwise Ok(Builtin { op, supplied: [] }) when builtin_named(x) is Some(op); otherwise Err(UnboundVariable(x)). A binding thus shadows a builtin’s name.
  2. (binders and lexical capture) Let { name: x, value: e₁, body: e₂ } evaluates e1​ in σ to a runtime A (a value or a function) and e2​ in σ[x↦A]; Lambda(x, b) evaluates to a closure capturing σ; applying Closure { x, b, σ₀ } to a runtime A evaluates b in σ0​[x↦A], whatever environment the application is evaluated in and wherever the closure was bound or passed; a Match arm’s body is evaluated in σ overridden by its pattern’s bindings, each a Runtime::Value. σ[x↦A] replaces any earlier binding of x, so the innermost enclosing binder of a name determines its denotation.
  3. (curried and partial builtins)
    1. a node Builtin(op, [e₁, …, eₙ]) with n<k evaluates e1​,…,en​ left to right to runtimes A1​,…,An​, returning the first refusal, and is Builtin { op, supplied: [A₁, …, Aₙ] };
    2. applying Builtin { op, supplied: s } to a runtime A gives Builtin { op, supplied: s ++ [A] } when ∣s∣+1<k, and otherwise the saturated application of op to node_order(op, s ++ [A]), where node_order exchanges the first two arguments of Map, Filter and FlatMap (surface map f xs is the node [xs, f]), the first and third of Fold (surface fold f z xs is the node [xs, z, f]), and leaves every other operation’s arguments in place;
    3. the saturated application of a first-order op to runtimes B1​,…,Bk​ requires each, in order, to be a value (the first function gives NotAFunction) and is apply_builtin(op, [v₁, …, v_k]); of a higher-order op it requires B1​ to be a value (else NotAFunction) and a list (else TypeError { expected: "list", .. }), for Fold requires B2​ to be a value, and applies Bk​ as the function in the order of clause 6;
    4. (agreement) if F evaluates to Builtin { op, supplied: [] } and e1​,…,ek​, listed in surface order, each returns Ok when evaluated in σ, then the curried application Apply(…Apply(F, e₁)…, e_k) has the same outcome as the node Builtin(op, node_order(op, [e₁, …, e_k])); and for j<k the partial node Builtin(op, [e₁, …, e_j]) evaluates to the same partial builtin as Apply(…Apply(F, e₁)…, e_j).
  4. (lexical scope) if two runtime environments are related on FV(e) (Definitions used), then eval_runtime(e, σ) returns exactly when eval_runtime(e, σ') does, with related outcomes. In particular, if ρ and ρ′ agree on FV(e) then eval(e, ρ) == eval(e, ρ'); a closed expression evaluates alike in every environment; and a function’s body, whether the function was bound by a let, passed as an argument or returned, never reads a binding of the place where it is applied.
  5. (exact operations)
    1. a Literal evaluates to its value unchanged (a float keeps its stored bits), and a bound Variable, a present record Field and an in-range Index return the stored runtime or value unchanged;
    2. for op in Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Mod, Neg, Abs applied to its arity’s number of values, if some value is a Decimal, BigInt or Temporal, the result is Err(ExactArithmetic { op, operand }), with operand the type name of the first such value; no exact value is converted;
    3. on Int values a,b: Add, Sub, Mul return Int of a+b, a−b, ab when it lies in i64 and Overflow otherwise; Div returns DivisionByZero when b=0, else Int of the quotient truncated toward zero, or Overflow exactly when a= i64::MIN and b=−1; Mod returns DivisionByZero when b=0, else Int of the truncated remainder a−b⋅trunc(a/b), which always lies in i64 and is 0 for i64::MIN and −1, so Mod never returns Overflow; Neg and Abs return −a and ∣a∣, or Overflow when a is i64::MIN;
    4. (refusal order of the numeric binary builtins) Add, Sub, Mul and Div on two values check, in this order: (i) an exact operand, giving ExactArithmetic as in clause 5.2; (ii) the operand types, admitting only Int or Float on each side, any other pair giving TypeError { expected: "int|float", got } with got the type name of the left operand; (iii) for Div only, a zero divisor, giving DivisionByZero when both are Int and the divisor is 0, or when either is a Float and the divisor, read as binary64, equals 0 (either sign of zero); then (iv) the operation. Mod on two values checks (i) an exact operand, giving ExactArithmetic; (ii) whether both are Int, any other pair (a Float included) giving TypeError { expected: "int", got } with got the type name of the left operand; (iii) a zero divisor, giving DivisionByZero; then (iv) the remainder. So a division can refuse with DivisionByZero only when both operands are numbers of the admitted types: Div(Str("a"), Int(0)) is a TypeError, not a division by zero;
    5. for op in Lt, Lte, Gt, Gte on two values l,r that are not both temporals, at least one of which is a Decimal, BigInt or Temporal: when both are Int, BigInt or finite Decimal, the result is the boolean of the relation between the exact numbers ν^(l) and ν^(r) they denote; otherwise it is Err(TypeError { expected: "int|bigint|finite decimal, or comparable temporals", got: "incomparable exact values" });
    6. Equal(l, r), and the builtins Eq and Ne, on values l,r that both have canonical bytes return Bool(l == r) (negated for Ne), so equality is representation equality; when either value has no canonical bytes they return Err(UndefinedRepresentation).
  6. (evaluation order and typed refusals) every failure is a value of EvalError, and the first refusal in the following order is returned:
    • Apply(f, a): f, then a, then the application; applying a value is NotAFunction;
    • Let: the bound expression, then the body; Record and List: items left to right, each required to be a value, a record being the map its fields define, so a later field of one name replaces an earlier one; Field: the record, then the lookup (TypeError { expected: "record", .. } or FieldNotFound(field)); Index: the list, then the index, each a value, then the lookup (TypeError { expected: "list and int", .. } or IndexOutOfBounds { index, len }, a negative index included); Equal: left, then right; If: the condition, required to be Bool (else TypeError { expected: "bool", .. }), then one branch; Match: the scrutinee, then the arms in order (NonExhaustiveMatch when none accepts);
    • a first-order node with n≥k arguments: all n arguments left to right, each required to be a value, and only then the arity check, so a node with n>k whose arguments all evaluate to values is ArityMismatch { op, expected: k, got: n }, and one whose argument refuses returns that refusal first;
    • a higher-order node with n≥k arguments: the arity check first (ArityMismatch when n>k, before any argument is evaluated); then the list argument, required to be a value and a list; then, for Fold, the initial value (argument 2); then, only when the list has an item, the function (the last argument), once, before its first application; then the items in order, Map, Filter and FlatMap applying the function to each item, Filter requiring Bool and FlatMap a list of each result, and Fold applying the function to the accumulator and the result to the item; on an empty list the function is never evaluated, Map, Filter and FlatMap return the empty list and Fold its initial value;
    • an instance traversal builtin (Edge, Children, HasEdge, EdgeCount, Anchor, Edges) saturated with values is NoInstanceContext { op }; and an eval whose result is a closure or a partial builtin is NotAFunction.
  7. (bound names) if every free variable of e is bound by ρ or names a builtin, UnboundVariable never arises; and ArityMismatch arises only at a node with more arguments than its arity, never through a curried or partial application.

The production evaluator is required to equal eval exactly on the image of the test conversion expr_to_ref, the expressions of the domain written without Equal and If (production has neither form) whose literals are values a production literal denotes, in the empty environment, as checked by the named differential tests.

Outside the domain

Every expression and every environment is in the domain; each failure is one of the typed refusals named in clauses 1, 3, 5 and 6, or the operation’s own typed refusal from apply_builtin (Overflow, DivisionByZero, InvalidDecimal, FloatNotRepresentable, UndefinedRepresentation, TypeError). A function-valued result is not a value and is refused with NotAFunction. The production evaluator also carries evaluation budgets, refused as StepLimitExceeded, DepthExceeded and ListLengthExceeded, which have no counterpart in the definition; an input that exhausts a budget is outside the domain on which production is compared. The definition may not return on some inputs, for instance the self-application Apply(Lambda(x, Apply(Variable(x), Variable(x))), Lambda(x, Apply(Variable(x), Variable(x)))); clause 4 relates two evaluations in that case too, and no other clause asserts a result for an evaluation that does not return.

Definitions used

  • A runtime is Runtime::Value(v), Runtime::Closure { parameter, body, environment } with an environment of runtimes, or Runtime::Builtin { op, supplied } with a list of runtimes; a closure or a partial builtin is a function. Every runtime is a finite tree, so definitions by recursion on runtimes are well founded. An outcome is Ok(R) for a runtime or Err(ε) with ε: EvalError. Runtime::value maps Value(v) to Ok(v) and a function to Err(NotAFunction), and eval(e, ρ) is eval_runtime in the lifted environment followed by value.
  • arity(op) and builtin_named(name) are the reference tables of those names. apply_builtin checks its argument count against expected_arity(op), which equals arity(op) for every operation: the two tables list the same operations at 1 and at 3 and every other operation at 2.
  • apply_runtime(F, A): a closure as in clause 2; a partial builtin as in clause 3.2, its saturated case calling apply_saturated; a value gives NotAFunction. apply_saturated(op, B) is clause 3.3; its higher-order case calls higher_order with the already evaluated function. eval_builtin_expr and eval_higher_order evaluate a node as in clauses 3.1 and 6, and higher_order obtains the function through next(), which calls its thunk once, at the first item.
  • Bound variables of a pattern: BV of Wildcard and Literal is empty, of Variable(x) is {x}, and of Record, List and Constructor is the union over their subpatterns. Free variables: FV(Literal)=∅; FV(Variable(x))={x}; FV(Lambda(x,b))=FV(b)∖{x}; FV(Let{x,e1​,e2​})=FV(e1​)∪(FV(e2​)∖{x}); FV(Match{s,[(pi​,bi​)]})=FV(s)∪⋃i​(FV(bi​)∖BV(pi​)); for the other forms, the union over the immediate subexpressions.
  • Related runtimes, R≈R′, by recursion on the runtime tree: equal values; Closure { p, b, σ } and Closure { p, b, σ' } with σ≈FV(b)∖{p}​σ′; Builtin { op, s } and Builtin { op, s' } with lists of one length related pointwise. No two runtimes of different kinds are related. Environments are related on a set S, σ≈S​σ′, when every x∈S is unbound in both or bound in both to related runtimes. Related outcomes are equal errors or Ok of related runtimes. The relation is symmetric, by induction on the runtime tree.
  • The call tree of a call eval_runtime(e, σ) that returns is the finite tree of nested eval_runtime calls it makes, directly or through the helper functions above; its height is the length of its longest branch.
  • The definition is deterministic: eval_runtime reads only its arguments, so one expression in one environment has one outcome.
  • match_pattern(p, v, β) accepts any value for Wildcard; for Variable(x) binds x to v when x is unbound in β and otherwise accepts exactly when v is representation-equal to β(x), so a repeated name matches equal values only; for Literal(w) accepts exactly when v is representation-equal to w; for Record requires a record (an Unknown or an Opaque value) holding every named field and matches each in order; for List requires a list of the pattern’s length and matches item by item; and for Constructor(c, [p₀, …, pₙ₋₁]) requires an Unknown value whose field $tag is Str(c) and whose fields $0, …, $(n-1) exist and match p0​,…,pn−1​ in order, other fields being ignored. An Opaque value never matches a constructor pattern, whatever its fields; a production record literal is converted to Unknown, so the differential image of a constructor match is unaffected.
  • ν^, exact_decimal, compare, the canonical-byte domain D and representation, as in the reference value module, with ν^ of Int(v) the integer v, of BigInt the number (−1)negative⋅significand⋅10zeros, and of a finite Decimal its ν of L-values-10; D is the domain of L-values-13.
  • Rust’s checked_add, checked_sub, checked_mul, checked_div, checked_neg and checked_abs on i64 return the mathematical result (division truncating toward zero) when it lies in i64 and is defined, and None otherwise. On i128, % is the truncated remainder, exact for operands from i64, and i64::try_from succeeds exactly on values in i64.

Proof

  1. Clause 1. The Variable arm returns a clone of σ(x) when bound, else Builtin { op, supplied: [] } when builtin_named(x) is Some(op), else UnboundVariable(x). In eval, a bound σ(x) is Value(ρ(x)).
  2. Clause 2. The Let arm evaluates value to a runtime without calling value, clones σ, inserts x↦A (replacing any binding) and evaluates the body there. The Lambda arm returns Closure { x, b, σ }. The Apply arm evaluates function and argument to runtimes and calls apply_runtime, whose closure case inserts the parameter into the captured environment and evaluates the body there, reading no other environment. eval_match evaluates an arm’s body in a clone of σ extended by the bindings wrapped as Runtime::Value, extend replacing existing names.
  3. Clauses 3.1 to 3.3. eval_builtin_expr with n<k collects eval_runtime of each argument in order into a Result, which stops at the first error, and returns Builtin { op, supplied }. apply_runtime on Builtin { op, s } pushes A and returns the partial builtin while the length is below k; since every partial builtin is created with fewer than k arguments and grows by one per application, the length at saturation is exactly k, and apply_saturated(op, node_order(op, ·)) is called, node_order swapping as stated. apply_saturated for a first-order op maps value over the arguments in order, stopping at the first function, and calls apply_builtin; for a higher-order op it takes the first argument through value, checks it is a list, takes the second through value for Fold, takes the last as the function, and calls higher_order.
  4. Clause 3.4. Determinism gives ei​ the outcome Ok(A_i) wherever it is evaluated in σ. By induction on j, Apply(…Apply(F, e₁)…, e_j) evaluates F, then e1​,…,ej​ in order, and for j<k is Builtin { op, [A₁, …, A_j] } by step 3; the partial node with the same arguments is the same partial builtin by clause 3.1. At j=k the curried application is apply_saturated(op, node_order(op, [A₁, …, A_k])). For a first-order op, node_order is the identity and the node Builtin(op, [e₁, …, e_k]) evaluates each ei​ to Ai​, maps value in order, stopping at the same first function, and calls apply_builtin on the same values (its arity check passes in both, as expected_arity(op) = k). For a higher-order op, the node with arguments node_order(op, [e₁, …, e_k]) has length k, so eval_higher_order takes the list argument to the same value as apply_saturated does, performs the same list check, takes Fold’s initial value to the same value, and passes higher_order a thunk that evaluates the function argument, which by determinism returns the same Ok(A_f) that apply_saturated passes directly; higher_order calls its thunk at most once, before the first application, so both runs make the same applications to the same runtimes.
  5. Pattern bindings. By induction on the pattern, a successful match_pattern(p, v, β) leaves every name of BV(p) bound in β and never removes a binding (Variable finds or inserts; Record, List, Constructor need every subpattern to succeed). From the empty map its success and bindings depend only on p and v.
  6. Auxiliary facts for clause 4. (a) If R≈R′ then R.value() and R'.value() are equal, since related values are equal and related functions both give NotAFunction; likewise mapping value over two pointwise related lists stops at the same position with the same outcome. (b) If σ≈S​σ′ and A≈A′, then σ[x↦A]≈S∪{x}​σ′[x↦A′], and extension by one map of value bindings preserves relatedness on its domain. (c) node_order applies one permutation to two pointwise related lists, which stay pointwise related.
  7. Clause 4, the induction. By induction on the height n of the call tree: for all e,σ,σ′ with σ≈FV(e)​σ′, if eval_runtime(e, σ) returns with height n then eval_runtime(e, σ') returns a related outcome; symmetry of ≈ gives the converse, so one returns exactly when the other does. Every nested call, including a closure body run by apply_runtime and a function argument run by the thunk of eval_higher_order, lies in the call tree at smaller height. The application step: if F≈F′ and A≈A′ then apply_runtime(F, A) and apply_runtime(F', A') give related outcomes. Values give NotAFunction in both. Related closures give, by 6(b), environments related on FV(b), and the hypothesis applies to the body. Related partial builtins Builtin { op, s }, Builtin { op, s' } have one length, so both stay partial with related lists, or both saturate; then by 6(c) apply_saturated receives related lists, and its first-order case gives equal outcomes by 6(a), while its higher-order case takes related list arguments to the same value or the same refusal, related initial values likewise, related functions, and runs higher_order, whose applications to equal items go through the application step with related functions.
  8. Clause 4, the cases. Literal: one value. Variable(x): x∈FV(e), so it is bound in both to related runtimes, or unbound in both, when both give the same partial builtin with no arguments or the same UnboundVariable. Lambda(x, b): the captured environments are related on FV(b)∖{x}=FV(e). Apply(f, a): the hypothesis on f and a gives related runtimes or one first error, and the application step concludes. Let: related bound runtimes, then 6(b) and the hypothesis on the body. Record, List, Field, Index, Equal, If: each part’s outcome is related, hence equal after value by 6(a); the arm computes a function of those values and of syntax (representation, the lookups), If continues with one branch, and collections stop at the same first error. Match: one scrutinee value, the same arm and bindings by step 5, and environments related on FV(bi​) because FV(bi​)∖BV(pi​)⊆FV(e) and both read β elsewhere. Builtin node: the branch (n<k, higher-order, first-order) depends on syntax only; a partial node gives pointwise related supplied lists; a first-order node gives equal values or the same first refusal, then the same apply_builtin call; a higher-order node performs the same arity check, gets the same list and initial value, and its thunks evaluate the function argument in related environments, giving related functions by the hypothesis, after which the application step applies. Every arm is covered. The consequences follow as stated: lifts of environments agreeing on FV(e) are related on it, value gives equal results by 6(a), any two environments are related on the empty set, and step 2 shows that a function’s body reads only its captured environment and its parameter.
  9. Clause 5. A literal, a bound variable, a present field and a selected item are returned as clones, equal to their originals. apply_builtin checks the arity, then dispatches Add, Sub, Mul, Div to numeric_binop, Mod to integer_remainder, Neg, Abs to numeric_unary; each first calls exact_arithmetic, which returns ExactArithmetic { op, operand } for the first exact value in order. On two Ints, numeric_binop returns DivisionByZero for Div with b=0 and otherwise maps checked_add, checked_sub, checked_mul or checked_div to Int or Overflow; checked_div with b=0 is None only for i64::MIN and −1, whose quotient 263 is outside i64. integer_remainder returns DivisionByZero for b=0 and otherwise i64::try_from(i128::from(a) % i128::from(b)); the i128 remainder is the exact truncated remainder, of magnitude below ∣b∣≤263, hence in i64, so the conversion always succeeds and Overflow is never returned; for i64::MIN and −1 it is 0. numeric_unary maps checked_neg or checked_abs, None only at i64::MIN. Clause 5.4 is the order of the branches: numeric_binop and integer_remainder call exact_arithmetic before their match; numeric_binop’s match has the arms (Int, Int), (Int, Float), (Float, Int), (Float, Float) and a final (other, _) arm returning type_error("int|float", other) with other the left operand, and the zero test for Div lies inside the numeric arms only (in the (Int, Int) arm on b=0, and in float_binop on right == 0.0, which holds for both zeros, the Int divisor having been converted by int_as_f64, which maps 0 to 0.0); integer_remainder’s match has the arms (Int, Int(0)) returning DivisionByZero, (Int, Int) returning the remainder, and (other, _) returning type_error("int", other), so a non-Int operand reaches the type error before any zero test. Clause 5.5: compare handles two temporals first; otherwise, with an exact operand, exact_decimal maps Int(v) (through v.to_string() and parse_decimal, digits of ∣v∣, exponent 0, sign of v), BigInt and a finite Decimal to decimals denoting ν^, and anything else to None, giving the stated TypeError; the result left.cmp_numeric(&right) is cmp(ν^(l),ν^(r)) by L-values-10, mapped to is_lt, not is_gt, is_gt, not is_lt. Clause 5.6: both sites call representation, which by L-values-13 (property 4) is Some(l == r) on D and None otherwise, giving UndefinedRepresentation.
  10. Clause 6. The result type is Result<Value, EvalError>. The order is read off the arms: ? sequences Apply, Let, Field, Index, Equal, If, Match in the stated order; collect into a Result stops at the first failing item; eval_builtin_expr checks n<k first, then dispatches a higher-order node to eval_higher_order, which checks n=k (here n>k) before evaluating anything, evaluates argument 1 through value and checks it is a list, evaluates Fold’s argument 2 through value, and hands higher_order the thunk of the last argument; higher_order calls next() inside the loop over items, so the thunk runs once, at the first item, and never on an empty list, after which Map, Filter, FlatMap and Fold return the empty list or the initial value. A first-order node with n≥k maps every argument through eval_runtime and value before apply_builtin, whose first act is the arity check. apply_builtin returns NoInstanceContext { op } for the traversal operations. eval applies value to the result.
  11. Clause 7. Call a closure closed when every name of FV(b)∖{p} is bound in its environment or names a builtin, a partial builtin closed when its supplied runtimes are, and an environment closed when all its runtimes are. By induction on the call tree, every call eval_runtime(e', σ) made while evaluating such an input has every free variable of e′ bound in σ or naming a builtin, with σ closed, and returns closed runtimes: each arm extends its environment exactly at the names its binder removes from the free variables (by step 5 for Match), a Lambda captures an environment covering FV(b)∖{x} up to builtin names, and apply_runtime on a closed closure runs its body in such an environment. So the Variable arm always finds a binding or a builtin. ArityMismatch is returned only by the arity checks of eval_higher_order and apply_builtin; the first fires only for a node with n>k, and the second receives n values from a first-order node with n≥k or exactly k values from a saturated partial builtin (step 3), so it fires only for a node with n>k.

Exact temporal parsing preserves the accepted lexeme

Statement

For every descriptor F: TemporalLexicalForm and every string text:

  1. every value c in parse_candidates(k, text), for any form k, satisfies c.to_string() == text, and so does the value obtained from c by replacing a Local offset with Zulu(Unwritten) or with Fixed(m, Unwritten) for any m;
  2. if parse_as(F, text) = Some(v), then v.to_string() == text and v.lexical_form() == Some(F).

Hence parse_display(F, text) is true exactly when parse_as(F, text) is Some.

Outside the domain

  • When no standard parse of text has the descriptor F, or more than one does, parse_as(F, text) is None and parse_display(F, text) is false; production Temporal::parse_as returns None in the same cases.
  • An offset text whose four-byte body has a multi-byte character across byte 2, such as +aé1, is refused: body.get(..2) returns None there, so parse_offset (production parse_written_offset) returns None, the cut contributes no candidate, and the text is refused like any other unaccepted text. Every input thus ends in a value or in None; neither reader panics.

Definitions used

  • parse_offset, parse_year, parse_date_body, parse_seconds, parse_time_body, splits and parse_candidates as defined in the reference module temporal.
  • Display for Offset, write_date, write_time and Display for Temporal, as defined there. For an integer n<100, {n:02} is the unique two-character decimal string with value n.
  • digits_n(s, 2) = Some(n) holds exactly when s is two ASCII digits spelling n, so {n:02} is s in that case.
  • parse_as(F, text): the infinity branch when F.infinity is Some; otherwise the candidates of parse_candidates(F.kind, text), each with a Local offset replaced by F.offset when F.offset is an unwritten offset, filtered by lexical_form() == Some(F), returned only when exactly one survives.

Proof

  1. Offset lemma: parse_offset(s) = Some(o) implies o.to_string() == s. The cases of parse_offset are these. (i) "", "Z", "z" give Local, Zulu(Upper), Zulu(Lower), displayed as "", "Z", "z". (ii) Otherwise s is a sign then body. With three :-pieces h,m,q of two digits each, h≤23 and m,q≤59, the following subcases apply. When q=0 and 60h+m=0 with sign -, the value is NegZero(ExtendedSeconds), displayed -00:00:00, which is s because two digits spelling 0 are 00. When q=0 otherwise, the value is Fixed(±(60h+m), ExtendedSeconds), whose display writes the sign - exactly when the minutes are negative (that is, sign - and 60h+m>0), then h and m recovered as the quotient and remainder of 60h+m by 60 (valid as m≤59), then :00. When q=0, the value is FixedSeconds(±(3600h + 60m + q)), nonzero, whose display writes the same sign and recovers h,m,q as ∣x∣/3600, ∣x∣mod3600/60 and ∣x∣mod60. With two pieces, the result is Extended, displayed {sign}{h:02}:{m:02} (or -00:00 for NegZero(Extended)). Otherwise, a body of four bytes whose halves body.get(..2) and body.get(2..) are both Some and two digits each, that is a body of four digits, gives Basic, displayed {sign}{h:02}{m:02}. Otherwise, two digits give HourOnly with m=0, displayed {sign}{h:02}, the minutes being 60h. In every numeric case the written sign + with zero minutes gives Fixed(0, form), displayed with + because 0 is not negative.
  2. Year lemma: parse_year(s) = Some(Y) implies that write_date writes s for the year Y. s is an optional - and a digit string body of length 4, or of length above 4 with a nonzero first digit; ∣Y.value∣ is the number body spells and Y.width is its length. With length 4, {:04} reproduces body; with a nonzero first digit the number has exactly body.len() digits and {:0w$} reproduces body. write_date writes - when the value is negative or negative_zero is set: with the sign written, the value is negative when the magnitude is positive and negative_zero is set when it is zero; without it, the value is nonnegative and negative_zero is false.
  3. Date lemma: parse_date_body(s) = Some(d) implies write_date(d) == s. The cases: --- then two digits gives (None, None, Some(day)), written ---{day:02}; -- then rest with a - gives month and day from the two sides of the first -, written --{m:02}-{day:02}; -- then rest without - gives (None, Some(m), None), written --{m:02}; otherwise s is an optional - and body, and body.splitn(3, '-') yields the year part, then possibly the month part, then possibly the day part, so a day is present only with a month, and write_date writes the year (step 2), then -{m:02} and -{day:02} for the parts present, which is s. The final valid_date check does not change d.
  4. Seconds lemma: parse_seconds(r) = Some((q, f)) implies that {q:02} followed by .f when f is nonempty equals r. Without a ., f is empty and r is two digits; with a ., the part after it is nonempty, all digits, and equal to f.
  5. Time lemma: parse_time_body(s) = Some(t) implies write_time(t) == s. The cases: -- then seconds gives (None, None, Some(q)), written -- and step 4; - then m:rest gives (None, Some(m), Some(q)), written -{m:02}: and step 4; - then two digits gives (None, Some(m), None), written -{m:02}; otherwise s.splitn(3, ':') gives an hour, possibly a minute, and possibly seconds, a later part existing only after an earlier one, and write_time writes {h:02}, {h:02}:{m:02} or {h:02}:{m:02}: with step 4 respectively. The range filter does not change t.
  6. Clause 1 for the candidates. If text is infinity or -infinity, the only candidate for Date or DateTime is an infinity, whose display is that spelling. There is no candidate for Time, so the clause holds vacuously in that case. Otherwise each candidate comes from one cut of splits, with body text[..cut] and offset text[cut..]. For the date form the display is write_date(d) then the offset display, which by steps 3 and 1 is text[..cut] then text[cut..]. The time form is the same with step 5. For the date-time form, at is the first byte of T, t or space in the body; these are one-byte characters, so the body is body[..at], the separator byte and body[at+1..], and the display writes the date (step 3), the separator character recorded from that byte, the time (step 5) and the offset (step 1).
  7. Clause 1 for the substitution. The displays of Local, Zulu(Unwritten) and Fixed(m, Unwritten) are all empty (the first two by the first arm of Display for Offset, the third because numeric writes nothing for OffsetForm::Unwritten), and the offset is the last thing Display for Temporal writes, so replacing Local by either unwritten offset leaves the display unchanged.
  8. Clause 2, infinity branch. parse_as returns a value only when text equals the spelling of F.infinity, and that value is an infinity of the same sign, whose display is that spelling; the closing filter requires lexical_form() == Some(F).
  9. Clause 2, finite branch. The returned value is a candidate of parse_candidates(F.kind, text), possibly with its offset replaced as in step 7, that passed the filter lexical_form() == Some(F). By steps 6 and 7 its display is text. The equivalence for parse_display follows from its definition parse_as(F, text).is_some_and(|v| v.to_string() == text) and clause 2.

Temporal display parses to the same value

Statement

For every value v: Temporal with v.well_formed(), v.lexical_form() is Some(F) for a descriptor F, and parse_as(F, &v.to_string()) == Some(v). Hence display_parse(v) is true for every well-formed v, including reduced, front-truncated and infinite values and values with an unwritten offset.

Outside the domain

  • A value with well_formed() false has lexical_form() = None, so display_parse is false for it; production Temporal::lexical_form likewise returns None, and production deserialization refuses such a value with the error “a noncanonical temporal representation”.
  • No well-formed value is refused: the statement covers every value of the carrier.

Definitions used

  • well_formed, form, lexical_form, parse_offset, parse_year, parse_date_body, parse_seconds, parse_time_body, splits, parse_candidates, parse_as, Display for Offset, write_date, write_time and Display for Temporal, as defined in the reference module temporal.
  • An unwritten offset: Zulu(Unwritten) or Fixed(m, Unwritten); every other offset is written. By well_formed, NegZero(Unwritten) is not admitted.
  • The written offset text of v: v.offset.to_string() when the offset is written, and the empty string otherwise.
  • Clause 1 of Exact temporal parsing preserves the accepted lexeme: every candidate of parse_candidates(k, text), with or without a Local offset replaced by an unwritten one, displays as text.

Proof

  1. lexical_form is Some. For a well-formed v, form() is Some: an infinity returns its form, and a finite well-formed value has a date or a time, since well_formed returns false when form() is None. lexical_form thus returns Some(F) with F.kind = v.form(), the date and time shapes and separator of v, F.offset = v.offset and F.infinity the sign of v’s infinity, if any. Let text = v.to_string().
  2. Infinite v. Then text is infinity or -infinity, the spelling of F.infinity, so parse_as takes its infinity branch and builds Temporal::infinite(sign, F.kind, F.offset). F.kind is not Time because well_formed excludes a time infinity, so the result has no date, time or separator, the offset of v and the infinity (sign, F.kind); by well_formed this is v. Its descriptor is F, so the filter keeps it and the result is Some(v).
  3. Finite v: text is not an infinity spelling, because every admitted finite shape writes at least one two-digit field, so parse_candidates(F.kind, text) takes the branch of the form F.kind.
  4. Offset inverse: for every written offset o admitted by well_formed, parse_offset(o.to_string()) = Some(o). Cases: Local gives "" and back. Zulu(Upper) and Zulu(Lower) give Z and z and back. Fixed(m, Extended) gives the sign (- exactly when m<0), then ∣m∣/60 and ∣m∣mod60 as two digits each, which are at most 23 and 59 because ∣m∣<1440; parse_offset reads two pieces and returns Fixed(m, Extended), the sign + with m=0 giving Fixed(0, Extended). Fixed(m, Basic) is the same without :, read through the four-digit branch. Fixed(m, HourOnly) writes only the hour, and well_formed requires mmod60=0, so the hour-only branch returns minutes 60⋅∣m∣/60=∣m∣ with the sign. Fixed(m, ExtendedSeconds) writes :00 as a third piece, read back with q=0 as Fixed(m, ExtendedSeconds). FixedSeconds(x) with ∣x∣<86400 and xmod60=0 writes three pieces whose last is nonzero, read back as FixedSeconds(x). NegZero(f) for each admitted form writes -00:00, -0000, -00 or -00:00:00, read back as NegZero of the same form.
  5. Date inverse: for the date part d of a well-formed value, parse_date_body(write_date(d)) = Some(d). well_formed admits six shapes. (false, false, true) is written ---DD and read by the first branch; (false, true, false) as --MM, read by the second branch without a - in the rest; (false, true, true) as --MM-DD, read by the second branch with the split at the first -. A shape with a year writes an optional - and then digits, so it never starts with -- and reaches the third branch; the year digits have length width, which well_formed fixes at the maximum of 4 and the number of digits of ∣y∣, so the length is 4 or the first digit is nonzero, and parse_year returns the same value, negative_zero (the - is written exactly when the value is negative or negative_zero is set, and well_formed sets negative_zero only on year 0) and width. The month and day, in 1..12 and 1..31, are written as two digits and read back, and valid_date holds by well_formed.
  6. Time inverse: for the time part t of a well-formed value, parse_time_body(write_time(t)) = Some(t). The six admitted shapes are written HH, HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, -MM:SS, -MM and --SS, the shapes with a second followed by . and the fraction when it is nonempty (well_formed forbids a fraction without a second and requires its bytes to be digits). Each is read back by the corresponding branch of parse_time_body, the seconds through parse_seconds, and the range check holds because well_formed bounds the hour by 23, the minute by 59 and the second by 60.
  7. Existence. Let cut be text.len() minus the length of the written offset text of v. Then text[cut..] is that text, which parse_offset reads as v.offset by step 4 when the offset is written, and as Local when it is unwritten (the empty string). The body text[..cut] is the display of the date, separator and time of v. For the date and time forms, steps 5 and 6 read the fields back. For the date-time form, neither the date nor the time display contains T, t or a space, so the first such byte is the separator, and steps 5 and 6 read both sides; the time has an hour and the date is full or day-only by well_formed, so the closure returns them. The candidate at cut thus equals v, except that an unwritten offset of v appears as Local, which parse_as replaces by F.offset = v.offset. Its descriptor is F, so it survives the filter.
  8. Uniqueness of the survivor. Let c survive. Then lexical_form(c) = Some(F), so c is well formed with the shapes, separator, offset and infinity of v, and by clause 1 of L-values-15 c.to_string() == text. The offset of c equals that of v, so both displays end with the same offset text, and the remaining prefixes are equal. For the date-time form the separator character is the first occurrence of that character in the prefix, as in step 7, so the date displays agree and the time displays agree. Given the shape, a well-formed date display determines its fields: without a year it is ---DD, --MM or --MM-DD, two-digit fields at fixed positions; with a year, each present month or day takes three final characters -NN, and the rest is the year, whose sign is the first character and whose digits give the magnitude and the width. A well-formed time display likewise determines its fields: each present field is two digits at a position fixed by the shape, and the fraction is what follows the ., empty when there is none. Hence c = v.
  9. One survivor. parse_offset never returns an unwritten offset, and parse_as substitutes only a Local offset, so a survivor’s cut is text.len() when F.offset is unwritten, and text.len() minus the length of F.offset.to_string() otherwise. In both cases the cut is the one of step 7, and splits produces at most one candidate per cut. Thus exactly one value survives, matches.next().is_none() holds after it, and parse_as(F, text) = Some(v).

Temporal comparison reverses with its arguments

Statement

Let T be the set of values v: Temporal with v.well_formed(). For all a,b∈T:

  1. comparable(a, b) == comparable(b, a);
  2. cmp_chronological(b, a) == cmp_chronological(a, b).map(Ordering::reverse).

So cmp_chronological(a, b) is None exactly when cmp_chronological(b, a) is None, and when the two values are comparable their comparison reverses with the arguments, with no exception.

Outside the domain

  • An incomparable pair is refused with None in both orders, by clause 1; production Temporal::cmp_chronological refuses the same pairs.
  • A value with well_formed() false is outside the carrier; it can be built only by assigning public fields, lexical_form and canonical_bytes return None for it, and production deserialization refuses it with the error “a noncanonical temporal representation”.

Definitions used

  • comparable(a, b): false when a.offset.is_zoned() != b.offset.is_zoned(); otherwise, when either value is an infinity, a.form() == b.form(); otherwise a.shape() == b.shape() and, when a is truncated, a.offset.minutes() == b.offset.minutes().
  • cmp_chronological, order_key, cmp_fraction, shape, form and is_truncated as defined in the reference module temporal. A finite value is truncated when it has a date without a year, or no date and a time without an hour.
  • Ordering::reverse maps Less to Greater, Greater to Less and Equal to itself; it is an involution and sends Equal and only Equal to Equal.
  • p.then_with(f) is p when p is not Equal, and f() otherwise.
  • The order of TemporalInfinity is the derived one, Negative < Positive. The order of String and of Vec<i128> is lexicographic: at the first index where the two sequences differ, the elements decide (bytes, respectively integers, by size); if there is no such index, the shorter is less, and sequences of equal length are equal.
  • Clause 2 of Comparable temporals follow chronological order: on comparable pairs the result is never None.

Proof

  1. Clause 1, case analysis on the three branches of comparable. (i) The zoning test compares a.offset.is_zoned() with b.offset.is_zoned() by equality, which is symmetric. (ii) When the zonings agree and either value is an infinity, the condition “either is an infinity” and the result a.form() == b.form() are both symmetric. (iii) When both are finite, the shape test is symmetric. If the shapes agree, then a.is_truncated() == b.is_truncated(), because for a finite value is_truncated reads only whether a date is present, whether it has a year and whether the hour is present, all of which are recorded in the shape; so the last conjunct is !t || μ(a) == μ(b) for a common truth value t, with μ for offset.minutes(), which is symmetric. If the shapes differ, both orders give false.
  2. Two identities. (a) For each of the three orders above, y.cmp(x) == x.cmp(y).reverse(): for TemporalInfinity and for integers this is the definition of a total order read in both directions; for sequences, the first differing index is the same in both orders and the element comparison there reverses, and when there is none, the shorter sequence is the same one in both orders, so Less and Greater exchange and Equal stays. (b) (p.then_with(f)).reverse() == p.reverse().then_with(|| f().reverse()): if p is not Equal, the left side is p.reverse(), and p.reverse() is not Equal, so the right side is p.reverse() too; if p is Equal, the left side is f().reverse(), and p.reverse() is Equal, so the right side is f().reverse().
  3. Incomparable pairs. By step 1, if comparable(a, b) is false then so is comparable(b, a), and cmp_chronological returns None in both orders; None.map(reverse) is None, so clause 2 holds.
  4. Comparable pairs, both infinities. Both results are Some, by clause 2 of L-values-12, namely Some(l.cmp(&r)) and Some(r.cmp(&l)), which are reverses by step 2(a).
  5. Comparable pairs, exactly one infinity. The arm (Some((Negative, _)), None) | (None, Some((Positive, _))) gives Less and the arm (Some((Positive, _)), None) | (None, Some((Negative, _))) gives Greater. Exchanging the arguments sends each alternative of the first arm to an alternative of the second and back: a negative infinity on the left becomes a negative infinity on the right, and a positive infinity on the right becomes a positive infinity on the left. So the two results are Less and Greater in some order, which are reverses.
  6. Comparable pairs, both finite. The two results are ka.cmp(&kb).then_with(|| cmp_fraction(&fa, &fb)) and the same with a and b exchanged, and order_key of a value does not depend on the other argument. By step 2(a), kb.cmp(&ka) == ka.cmp(&kb).reverse(). cmp_fraction(fb, fa) pads both strings to the same length max(∣fa∣,∣fb∣) as cmp_fraction(fa, fb) does and compares the same two padded strings in the other order, so by step 2(a) it is cmp_fraction(fa, fb).reverse(). By step 2(b), the whole result is the reverse.

Each temporal comparability class is a total preorder

Statement

Let T be the set of values v: Temporal with v.well_formed(). Comparability is not transitive: two truncated dates of one shape whose offsets differ in minutes are incomparable, yet each is comparable with every date infinity of their zoning. The order is thus stated on comparability classes (defined below), each a finite comparability class together with every infinity that applies to it. For each comparability class K:

  1. every pair a,b∈K satisfies comparable(a, b), so cmp_chronological(a, b) is Some;
  2. the relation a⪯b, defined as cmp_chronological(a, b) ∈{Some(Less), Some(Equal)}, is a total preorder on K: reflexive, transitive and total;
  3. cmp_chronological(a, b) == Some(Equal) exactly when a⪯b and b⪯a, and cmp_chronological(a, b) == Some(Less) exactly when a⪯b and not b⪯a.

Moreover: (4) every comparable pair a,b∈T lies in a common class; and (5) the order is coherent across classes: if two classes share elements a,b, they compare a and b the same way, since the comparison is cmp_chronological(a, b) in both. Because a truncated class is fixed by offset minutes, --50+00:00:30 and --50Z (offset seconds 30 and 0, minutes 0 and 0) lie in one class and compare Equal.

Outside the domain

  • Two values in no common class are incomparable by clause 4, and cmp_chronological refuses them with None in both orders (Temporal comparison reverses with its arguments).
  • A value with well_formed() false is outside the carrier; it can be built only by assigning public fields, lexical_form and canonical_bytes return None for it, and production deserialization refuses it with the error “a noncanonical temporal representation”.

Definitions used

  • comparable(a, b): false when the zonings differ; otherwise, when either value is an infinity, a.form() == b.form(); otherwise a.shape() == b.shape() and, when a is truncated, a.offset.minutes() == b.offset.minutes(). cmp_chronological, shape, form, is_truncated, Offset::is_zoned and Offset::minutes as defined in the reference module temporal; minutes is None for Local, and for FixedSeconds(x) it is x / 60 rounded toward zero. A finite shape is truncated when it has a date without a year, or no date and a time without an hour.
  • Finite comparability class. For the shape sh of a well-formed finite value, a zoning z∈{local,zoned} and a minute value m, which is None when z is local and an integer when z is zoned, C(sh,z,m) is the set of finite v∈T with v.shape() == sh, v.offset.is_zoned() equal to z and, when sh is truncated, v.offset.minutes() == m. When sh is not truncated, the condition on m is dropped, so C(sh,z,m) is the same set for every admissible m.
  • Comparability class: K(sh,z,m)=C(sh,z,m)∪J(form of sh,z), where J(k,z) is the set of infinities u∈T with u.form() == k and zoning z (empty when k is Time, since well_formed excludes a time infinity). The infinities of J(k,z) apply to every finite class of form k and zoning z.
  • The chronological key κ and its lexicographic order, from clause 2 of Comparable temporals follow chronological order: cmp_chronological(a, b) = Some(ord(κ(a), κ(b))) whenever comparable(a, b) holds.
  • A total preorder on a set: a reflexive, transitive relation under which every two elements are related in at least one direction.

Proof

  1. Clause 1. Let a,b∈K=K(sh,z,m). Both have zoning z, so the zoning test passes. If either is an infinity, comparable compares forms, and every member of K has the form of sh (a finite member through its shape, an infinity by the definition of J), so it holds. If both are finite, both have shape sh; if sh is truncated, both have offset minutes m, so the last conjunct holds; otherwise it holds outright. By clause 2 of L-values-12 the result is Some.
  2. By clause 1 and clause 2 of L-values-12, on K the comparator is a,b↦ Some(ord(κ(a), κ(b))).
  3. The key order is a total order on keys. Its first components are the integers 0, 1, 2; keys with first component 0 (or 2) are all equal; keys with first component 1 are triples whose second component is a tuple of integers ordered lexicographically, which is a total order, and whose third component is a rational number ordered by size. A lexicographic combination of total orders is a total order: two keys are equal exactly when all compared components are equal, and the first differing component decides, so reflexivity, antisymmetry, totality and transitivity follow componentwise.
  4. Clause 2. By step 2, a⪯b holds exactly when κ(a)≤κ(b). Reflexivity: κ(a)≤κ(a). Totality: one of κ(a)≤κ(b), κ(b)≤κ(a) holds by step 3. Transitivity: κ(a)≤κ(b)≤κ(c) gives κ(a)≤κ(c).
  5. Clause 3. By step 2, the result is Some(Equal) exactly when κ(a)=κ(b), which in a total order is κ(a)≤κ(b) and κ(b)≤κ(a); it is Some(Less) exactly when κ(a)<κ(b), which is κ(a)≤κ(b) and not κ(b)≤κ(a).
  6. Clause 4, every case of a comparable pair with common zoning z; let mz​ be None when z is local and 0 when z is zoned. Both finite: they share the shape sh, and when sh is truncated they share the offset minutes m, which is None exactly when z is local; both lie in C(sh,z,m), taking m=mz​ when sh is not truncated. One infinity u and one finite w: the forms agree, so u∈J(form of w,z) and both lie in K(shape of w,z,μ(w)), where μ(w) is None exactly when z is local. Both infinities: they share a form k, which is Date or DateTime by well_formed; take for sh the shape of a full date, respectively of a full date with a time with an hour, which is not truncated, and both lie in J(k,z)⊆K(sh,z,mz​).
  7. Clause 5 holds because membership in a class does not enter the definition of cmp_chronological. The examples. --50+00:00:30 has offset FixedSeconds(30), whose minutes are 30/60=0 rounded toward zero, and --50Z has minutes 0; both are zoned time-only values of the shape with only a second, so both lie in C(sh,zoned,0), and their keys are (1,(50),0), so the comparison is Equal by step 2. The truncated dates --04-12+02:00 and --04-12Z have minutes 120 and 0, so they are incomparable and lie in the distinct classes K(sh,zoned,120) and K(sh,zoned,0), both of which contain every zoned date infinity, comparable with each of them by step 1.

Chronological equality ignores written temporal form

Statement

Let T be the set of values v: Temporal with v.well_formed(), and call a,b∈T written-form variants, a≈b, when they agree on everything but how they are written (definition below). For all a,b,c∈T with a≈b:

  1. cmp_chronological(a, c) == cmp_chronological(b, c) and cmp_chronological(c, a) == cmp_chronological(c, b);
  2. cmp_chronological(a, b) == Some(Equal).

Moreover, a≈b does not imply a=b: two written-form variants differ under == whenever they differ in the separator, the case of Z, the written form of an offset of equal seconds, the sign written on year zero, or trailing zeros of the fraction (explicit pairs in step 6). Conversely, chronological equality is wider than written-form variance: values with different fields that denote one instant also compare Equal (step 7).

Outside the domain

  • A value with well_formed() false is outside the carrier; it can be built only by assigning public fields, lexical_form and canonical_bytes return None for it, and production deserialization refuses it.
  • Values that are not written-form variants are outside the hypothesis; their comparison is described by Comparable temporals follow chronological order, and an incomparable pair is refused with None.

Definitions used

  • comparable(a, b): false when exactly one of the two is local; otherwise, when either is an infinity, a.form() == b.form(); otherwise a.shape() == b.shape() and, when a is truncated, a.offset.minutes() == b.offset.minutes(). cmp_chronological, order_key, shape, form, is_truncated, Offset::is_zoned, Offset::seconds and Offset::minutes as defined in the reference module temporal.
  • val(x) for a digit string x=d1​⋯dn​: ∑i​di​10−i, and 0 for the empty string.
  • Written-form variants: a≈b when (i) a.infinity == b.infinity; (ii) a.shape() == b.shape(); (iii) a.offset.is_zoned() == b.offset.is_zoned() and a.offset.seconds() == b.offset.seconds(); (iv) the present year values, months, days, hours, minutes and seconds are equal; (v) the fractions fa​, fb​ (empty without a time) satisfy val(fa​)=val(fb​). The separator, the case of Z, the OffsetForm, the choice among Zulu, Fixed(0, _) and NegZero(_) for a zero offset, the negative_zero flag and trailing zeros of the fraction are left free.
  • The chronological key κ and clause 2 of Comparable temporals follow chronological order: cmp_chronological(x, y) = Some(ord(κ(x), κ(y))) when comparable(x, y), and None otherwise by its clause 1.

Proof

  1. For a zoned offset, minutes() is the quotient of seconds() by 60 rounded toward zero: Zulu(_) and NegZero(_) give 0 and 0; Fixed(m, _) gives 60m and m; FixedSeconds(x) gives x and x / 60 in i64, which rounds toward zero. A local offset gives None for both. Hence condition (iii) gives a.offset.is_zoned() == b.offset.is_zoned() and a.offset.minutes() == b.offset.minutes(), the only offset quantities comparable reads.
  2. Condition (ii), together with (i), gives a.form() == b.form() and a.is_truncated() == b.is_truncated(): form depends only on the infinity and on the presence of the date and time, and is_truncated only on the infinity and the presence of the date, its year and the hour.
  3. comparable(a, c) == comparable(b, c): its branches read from the first argument only the zoning and the offset minutes (step 1), whether it is an infinity (i), its form or shape ((ii) and step 2) and its truncation (step 2), which agree. comparable(c, a) == comparable(c, b) for the same reasons, since from the second argument it reads the zoning, whether it is an infinity, the form or shape and the offset minutes.
  4. κ(a)=κ(b). If both are infinities, (i) gives the same sign and so the same key. If both are finite, step 2 puts them in the same branch of order_key. In the truncated branch the key is the tuple of present fields, equal by (ii) and (iv). In the other branch the key is I=2(86400N+3600h+60m+min(s,59)−σ0​)+[s=60], where N depends on the year value, month and day, and σ0​ is seconds() or 0 for a local value; all are equal by (iii) and (iv), and negative_zero and the year width do not enter. The third key component is val of the fraction, equal by (v).
  5. Clauses 1 and 2. By step 3, cmp_chronological(a, c) and cmp_chronological(b, c) are both None, or both are Some of a comparison of keys, which agree by step 4; the same holds with the arguments exchanged. For clause 2, comparable(a, b) holds: the zonings agree, the forms (when an infinity is involved) or shapes agree, and the offset minutes agree by step 1. Then the result is Some(ord(κ(a), κ(b))) = Some(Equal) by step 4.
  6. Distinct variants. Each of the following pairs consists of well-formed values satisfying (i) to (v) and differing in one field, hence unequal under the derived ==: the date-times 2024-01-02T03:04:05Z and 2024-01-02t03:04:05Z (separator); …Z and …z (case of Z); …Z, …+00:00, …-00:00, …+0000, …+00, …+00:00:00 and the same date-time with offset Zulu(Unwritten) (zero offsets of seconds 0, all zoned); …+05:30 and …+0530 (Fixed(330, Extended) and Fixed(330, Basic)); the dates -0000 and 0000 (negative_zero on year 0, both of value 0 and width 4); the times 12:00:00.1 and 12:00:00.10 (val=1/10 for both). By clause 2 each pair compares Equal.
  7. Equality wider than variance. The values p = 2024-01-02T08:34:05+05:30 and q = 2024-01-02T03:04:05Z differ in hour, minute and offset seconds, so they are not variants. Both are finite, non-truncated, zoned, of one shape, so comparable(p, q) holds, and with N the day number of 2024-01-02, I(p)=2(86400N+28800+2040+5−19800)=2(86400N+11045) and I(q)=2(86400N+10800+240+5)=2(86400N+11045), with empty fractions; by L-values-12 the result is Some(Equal).
